### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-MKT

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-MKT  
CANONICAL NAME:      Market Data  
ARABIC NAME:         بيانات السوق  
CONTEXT CODE:        MKT  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Market Data Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Market Data ingestion and distribution is a foundational capability acquiring, validating, and streaming real-time quote ticks and order book snapshots. It guarantees a verified data baseline for all downstream pricing, valuation, and AI analytics.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for acquiring raw streaming tick feeds, bid-ask quotes, order book depth snapshots, and trade volumes from licensed exchange vendors, validating tick data quality, filtering corrupted ticks, and distributing normalized real-time quote feeds across Tradeora.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Acquisition of raw real-time price tick feeds, bid-ask quotes, and trade volume data from licensed exchange vendors.  
  - Real-time tick validation, outlier detection, zero-price filtering, and timestamp verification.  
  - Real-time order book depth snapshot aggregation (Level 1 and Level 2 quote depth).  
  - Normalization of disparate data vendor payload formats into standard internal quote streams.  
  - Management of market data ingestion stream health and vendor SLA monitoring.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Derived historical OHLCV price bar aggregation or adjusted price series (owned strictly by `CTX-PRC`).  
  - Security master metadata, ISIN generation, or listing status (owned strictly by `CTX-SEC`).  
  - Technical indicator computation such as RSI or Moving Averages (owned strictly by `CTX-TECH`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Market Data Engineering  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  System, Active Trader, Portfolio Manager, Risk Evaluator, Data Engineers  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `DataSource` (BDD Sec 9 Object 37) — Authoritative vendor feed provider entity and SLA metadata.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `MKT-DAT-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 1) — Real-Time Market Data Ingestion.  
  - `MKT-DAT-002` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 1) — Market Data Distribution.  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `MKT_PRICE_TICK_RECEIVED` (BDD Sec 12 Event 3) — Triggered when a validated real-time trade tick or quote update is ingested.  
  - `MKT_ORDER_BOOK_SNAPSHOT_CAPTURED` — Triggered when a new order book depth snapshot is validated.  
  - `MKT_DATA_FEED_DEGRADED` — Triggered when data vendor latency exceeds SLA boundaries.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `CAL_SESSION_STARTED` — Consumed from `CTX-SES` to activate real-time feed validation pipelines.  
  - `CAL_SESSION_CLOSED` — Consumed from `CTX-SES` to transition pipelines to end-of-day mode.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `Price Tick`: Real-time execution quote update snapshot.  
  - `Order Book Depth`: Snapshot of active bid and ask quotes at varying price levels.  
  - `DataSource`: External entity delivering market pricing feeds (UL Sec 2.2).  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 2: Historical market data is immutable once recorded; corrections must be appended as auditable adjustment records (BDD Sec 10 Rule 2).  
  - Rule 7: No financial data may be displayed without clear source attribution and execution timestamp (BDD Sec 10 Rule 7).  
  - Rule 18: Real-time quote stream latency must not exceed defined SLA boundaries (< 500ms) for active capabilities (BDD Sec 10 Rule 18).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `Price Tick` (raw execution tick) is distinct from `OHLCV` (aggregated price bar) and `Instrument`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 18 (tick latency SLA) and Rule 7 (source attribution) apply exclusively to feed ingestion.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `MKT_PRICE_TICK_RECEIVED` and `MKT_DATA_FEED_DEGRADED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive lifecycle owner of `DataSource` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Real-time tick streams operate on high-frequency sub-second lifecycles continuously during trading sessions.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Market Data Engineering.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-EXCH: Open Host Service | HARD | Requires venue MIC code.  
  - CTX-SEC: Open Host Service | HARD | Requires valid Instrument ID to qualify incoming ticks.  
  - CTX-SES: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes real-time session state to govern validation rules.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-PRC: Consumes raw price ticks to compute OHLCV bars and closing prices.  
  - CTX-ALRT: Consumes real-time price ticks to evaluate high-velocity price breakout rules.  
  - CTX-RISK: Consumes price tick streams to update intraday portfolio Value-at-Risk (VaR).  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:

[SUBDOMAIN CLASSIFICATION]  
  Domain Classification: Core Enabling  
  Classification Justification: Real-time market data ingestion and distribution is a foundational capability providing verified quote ticks for all platform analytics. It enforces strict sub-second latency SLAs (< 500ms) and quality validation across data vendor streams.  
  Business Differentiation: Sub-second ingestion latency, robust outlier filtering, and native multi-market normalization.  
  Competitive Advantage: YES — High-reliability data stream foundation prevents false price tick calculations.  
  Outsourcing Decision: PREFERRED | Rationale: Raw exchange tick streams are acquired from licensed market data vendors.  
  Engineering Investment Posture: INVEST ADEQUATELY  
  AI Investment Posture: LOW | Rationale: Automated anomaly detection algorithms for identifying corrupted or outlier price ticks.  
  Team Implication: High-performance data engineering team specializing in streaming architecture.  

[CONTEXT LIFECYCLE]  
  Status: Approved  

[CONTEXT DECISION RECORD]  
  CREATION DATE: 2026-07-21  
  DECISION MAKERS: Architecture Governance Board & Domain Architects  
  Problem Statement: Incoming raw data vendor tick streams contain noise, corrupted zero-prices, and varying payload formats requiring high-frequency normalization before reaching analytical models.  
  Decision: Established `CTX-MKT` as a Core Enabling Context owning real-time tick ingestion, data source SLA tracking, and raw quote distribution.  
  Discovery Evidence Summary: All 6 evidence types confirmed.  
  Alternatives Considered:  
    - Alternative 1: Merge into Pricing (`CTX-PRC`). Rejected: Ingestion operates on raw high-frequency tick streams; Pricing operates on derived historical bars and official closing prices.  
    - Alternative 2: Allow analytical microservices to ingest vendor feeds directly. Rejected: Violates Principle 33 (Single Source of Truth) and multiplies vendor licensing costs.  
  Known Limitations: Dependent on vendor network connectivity during market spikes.  
  Future Split Candidates: High-frequency Level 2 Order Book Depth context if depth analytics expand significantly in Phase 3.  
  Future Merge Candidates: None.  
  Trigger Conditions for Revision: Data vendor transitions from tick-based streaming to direct memory-mapped protocol architectures.

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-PRC

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-PRC  
CANONICAL NAME:      Pricing  
ARABIC NAME:         التسعير  
CONTEXT CODE:        PRC  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Market Data Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Pricing context compiles, aggregates, and stores authoritative historical price series, official exchange closing prices, intraday OHLCV bars, and corporate-action-adjusted price histories. It guarantees mathematical precision for portfolio valuations and quantitative models.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for aggregating raw price ticks into standardized time-interval bars (OHLCV), compiling official End-of-Day (EOD) closing prices, maintaining historical price databases, and computing adjusted price series to reflect historical corporate actions (splits, bonus shares).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Compilation and publishing of official End-of-Day (EOD) closing prices for all listed instruments.  
  - Aggregation of intraday price bars across standardized intervals (1-min, 5-min, 1-hour, 1-day OHLCV).  
  - Maintenance of immutable historical price databases across global markets.  
  - Calculation and maintenance of Adjusted Price series reflecting historical corporate action split factors (Rule 22).  
  - Computing technical price summary statistics (52-week high/low, daily turnover, volume-weighted average price - VWAP).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Real-time raw tick feed ingestion or data vendor stream failover (owned strictly by `CTX-MKT`).  
  - Announcement or approval of corporate action split ratios (owned strictly by `CTX-CORP`).  
  - Computation of momentum indicators like RSI or MACD (owned strictly by `CTX-TECH`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Chief Financial Valuation Architect  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  System, Long-Term Investor, Active Trader, Portfolio Manager, Quantitative Analyst  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `Price` (BDD Sec 9 Object 7) — Verified monetary valuation snapshot at a specific point in time.  
  - `OHLCV` (BDD Sec 9 Object 8) — Standardized aggregated price bar summarizing market action.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `MKT-DAT-003` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 1) — Technical Indicator Computation (base price series component).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `MKT_EOD_PRICES_PUBLISHED` (BDD Sec 12 Event 4) — Triggered when official closing prices are finalized for a trading day.  
  - `MKT_OHLCV_BAR_AGGREGATED` — Triggered when a historical price bar interval completes.  
  - `MKT_HISTORICAL_PRICES_ADJUSTED` — Triggered when price history is recalculated following a corporate action.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `MKT_PRICE_TICK_RECEIVED` — Consumed from `CTX-MKT` to update active OHLCV bar intervals.  
  - `CORP_SPLIT_EFFECTED` — Consumed from `CTX-CORP` to trigger historical price adjustments.  
  - `CAL_SESSION_CLOSED` — Consumed from `CTX-SES` to initiate EOD closing price finalized batch.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `Price`: Verified monetary valuation snapshot for an Instrument (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `OHLCV`: Aggregated price bar (Open, High, Low, Close, Volume).  
  - `Adjusted Price`: Historical price series recalculated to preserve percentage returns after corporate actions.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 2: Historical market data is immutable once recorded; corrections must be appended as auditable adjustment records (BDD Sec 10 Rule 2).  
  - Rule 5: A position cannot be valued without a verified price source and explicit timestamp (BDD Sec 10 Rule 5).  
  - Rule 22: Price adjustment calculations following stock splits or bonus shares must preserve historical percentage returns (BDD Sec 10 Rule 22).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `Price` (verified valuation record) is distinct from raw `Price Tick` and `Instrument`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 5 (verified price required for valuation) and Rule 22 (return-preserving adjustments) apply exclusively here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `MKT_EOD_PRICES_PUBLISHED` and `MKT_HISTORICAL_PRICES_ADJUSTED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive lifecycle owner of `Price` and `OHLCV` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — EOD prices and historical price series evolve on daily batch and historical adjustment lifecycles.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Chief Financial Valuation Architect.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-MKT: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes real-time price ticks to build price bars.  
  - CTX-SEC: Open Host Service | HARD | Requires Instrument reference metadata.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-PORT: Consumes EOD closing prices to compute daily portfolio NAV.  
  - CTX-VAL: Consumes verified price records to calculate current position market values.  
  - CTX-TECH: Consumes historical OHLCV series to compute technical indicators.  
  - CTX-FUND: Consumes closing prices to calculate P/E and Market Cap metrics.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:

    Violation Consequence: Rejection of adjustment factor application; recalculation required.

    Business Rationale: Preserves immutable audit trail for compliance and model verification.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Append-only persistent data layer policy.  
    Violation Consequence: System operation error on overwrite attempt.

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-CORP  
CANONICAL NAME:      Corporate Actions  
ARABIC NAME:         إجراءات الشركات

DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Market Data Cluster

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Corporate Actions context captures, validates, and processes corporate capital events (cash/stock dividends, stock splits, bonus shares, rights issues, mergers). It is essential for preserving historical valuation continuity and portfolio position accuracy across capital restructurings.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for capturing official corporate action disclosures from exchanges and issuing companies, calculating adjustment factors for price histories and position quantities, managing ex-date and record-date schedules, and broadcasting corporate action events to portfolio and pricing domains.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Tracking official corporate action announcements (cash dividends, stock splits, bonus shares, rights issues, spin-offs, mergers).  
  - Managing corporate action lifecycle states (Announced, Approved, Ex-Date Effective, Record Date, Completed, Cancelled).  
  - Calculating official price adjustment factors and position multiplier ratios following stock splits or bonus shares.  
  - Maintaining record date, ex-dividend date, announcement date, and pay date schedules for all listed corporate assets.  
  - Capturing dividend payment attributes (dividend per share, dividend currency, tax withholding rates).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Directly modifying user portfolio holdings or cash ledgers (owned strictly by `CTX-PORT` / `CTX-HOLD`).  
  - Recalculating historical price databases (owned strictly by `CTX-PRC`).  
  - Security master ticker creation or delisting operations (owned strictly by `CTX-SEC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Corporate Actions Operations Manager  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  System, Long-Term Investor, Portfolio Manager, Compliance Officer  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `Dividend` (BDD Sec 9 Object 9) — Distribution of corporate earnings allocated to eligible shareholders.  
  - `CorporateAction` (BDD Sec 9 Object 10) — Official capital event initiated by an issuing company.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `MKT-SEC-002` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 1) — Corporate Action Tracking.  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `CORP_DIVIDEND_ANNOUNCED` (BDD Sec 12 Event 5) — Triggered when an upcoming cash or stock dividend is disclosed.  
  - `CORP_SPLIT_EFFECTED` (BDD Sec 12 Event 6) — Triggered on ex-date when a stock split or bonus share ratio becomes effective.  
  - `CORP_ACTION_COMPLETED` — Triggered when corporate action distribution processing is finalized.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `INST_SECURITY_LISTED` — Consumed from `CTX-SEC` to enable corporate action tracking for newly listed asset.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `CorporateAction`: Official event initiated by an issuing company impacting outstanding securities (UL Sec 2.2).  
  - `Ex-Date`: Date on which a security begins trading without entitlement to the declared dividend or action.  
  - `Record Date`: Date on which an investor must be officially registered to receive a corporate distribution.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 9: Corporate actions must be reflected in portfolio valuations within one business day of official exchange confirmation (BDD Sec 10 Rule 9).  
  - Rule 22: Price adjustment calculations following stock splits or bonus shares must preserve historical percentage returns (BDD Sec 10 Rule 22).  
  - Rule 24: All corporate action events generate tamper-evident audit records (BDD Sec 10 Rule 24).

  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces all `CORP_` prefixed events (`CORP_DIVIDEND_ANNOUNCED`, `CORP_SPLIT_EFFECTED`).  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive lifecycle owner of `CorporateAction` and `Dividend` objects.

  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Corporate Actions Operations Manager.

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-MKT (Market Data):  
    Language difference: `Tick Size Rule` is an operational parameter table; `Price Tick` is a real-time execution snapshot.

    Object difference: OWNS Market Structure failover policies; does NOT own raw tick streams.  
    Event difference: Produces `MKT_FEED_FAILOVER_EXECUTED`; does NOT produce `MKT_PRICE_TICK_RECEIVED`.

    Language difference: `Market Structure` defines micro-structure parameters (tick sizes); `Exchange` defines macro venue identity.  
    Rule difference: Failover routing rules vs venue qualification rules.  
    Object difference: OWNS micro-structure routing policies; does NOT own `Exchange` or `Market`.  
    Event difference: Failover events occur on network degradation; Exchange onboarding occurs on venue addition.

  INV-01: Data feed failover execution MUST switch to secondary backup feed within 5 seconds of primary feed degradation (Rule 33 / BDD Policy 6).  
    Business Rationale: Protects platform uptime and user trust during primary vendor stream outages.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated failover router health check handler.  
    Violation Consequence: Triggers high-priority operational alarm to infrastructure team.  
  INV-02: Every listed Instrument MUST be bound to a valid Tick Size Table corresponding to its price band.  
    Business Rationale: Guarantees price rounding and order validation precision.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Invariant check on instrument parameters configuration.  
    Violation Consequence: Rejection of pricing updates failing tick size precision rules.  
  INV-03: Market structure parameter updates MUST carry explicit effective date timestamps.  
    Business Rationale: Ensures historical price bar compilation respects historical tick size rules.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Effective date indexing on parameter table records.  
    Violation Consequence: Parameter update rejection.

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-FUND  
CANONICAL NAME:      Fundamental Research  
ARABIC NAME:         البحوث الأساسية

VERSION:             1.0

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Differentiating  
  Justification:     Fundamental Research standardizes corporate balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow disclosures under IFRS and Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS). It parses quarterly earnings reports and executes mathematical Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) fair-value modeling, creating Tradeora's core fundamental valuation moat.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for extracting, standardizing, and modeling corporate financial statements, earnings announcements, and balance sheet metrics, computing standardized financial ratios, and building mathematical Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) intrinsic fair-value models.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Standardization and normalization of corporate balance sheets, income statements, and cash flow filings under IFRS and EAS.  
  - Parsing quarterly earnings releases, consensus EPS surprises, and corporate revenue guidance notes.  
  - Computation of mathematical Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) and Dividend Discount Model (DDM) fair-value estimates.  
  - Generation of valuation sensitivity matrices (varying WACC, terminal growth rates, and margins of safety).  
  - Standardized financial ratio trend modeling (P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, ROE, Debt-to-Equity, Free Cash Flow Yield).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Real-time stock price tick feeds or intraday OHLCV time bars (owned strictly by `CTX-MKT` / `CTX-PRC`).  
  - Quantitative factor score ranking across broad asset universes (owned strictly by `CTX-QUANT`).  
  - Qualitative news article sentiment scoring (owned strictly by `CTX-SENT`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Chief Fundamental Equity Research Analyst  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Long-Term Investor, Research Analyst, Portfolio Manager, Wealth Advisor  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `FinancialStatement` (BDD Sec 9 Object 11) — Normalized financial report detailing financial position over accounting period.  
  - `EarningsReport` (BDD Sec 9 Object 12) — Detailed disclosure summarizing quarterly financial results and surprises.  
  - `FairValueModel` (BDD Sec 9 Object 39) — Mathematical intrinsic valuation calculation payload.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `RES-FND-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 2) — Financial Statement Standardization (Primary Owner).

  - `RES_DCF_MODEL_EVALUATED` — Triggered when an intrinsic fair-value model calculation completes.

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-TECH

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-TECH  
CANONICAL NAME:      Technical Research  
ARABIC NAME:         التحليل الفني  
CONTEXT CODE:        TECH  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Financial Research Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Technical Research computes technical momentum, volatility, and volume indicators (RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, Moving Averages) across multi-timeframe OHLCV price series. It provides quantitative price context for active traders and screening engines.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for computing mathematical technical indicators, trend momentum scores, support/resistance levels, and volatility metrics across multiple timeframes, converting raw price series into structured technical analysis context.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Computation of standard technical momentum indicators (RSI, MACD, Stochastic Oscillator, CCI).  
  - Calculation of price volatility metrics (Bollinger Bands, Average True Range - ATR, Standard Deviation).  
  - Moving average cluster calculations (Simple, Exponential, Weighted Moving Averages across 20, 50, 200-day periods).  
  - Detection of technical support and resistance levels and trend channel boundaries.  
  - Volume-weighted price indicators (VWAP, On-Balance Volume - OBV, Accumulation/Distribution).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Derived historical OHLCV bar aggregation or closing price records (owned strictly by `CTX-PRC`).  
  - Specialized active trader strategy patterns like Order Blocks, Fair Value Gaps, or ICT/Wyckoff frameworks (owned strictly by `CTX-STRAT`).  
  - Generating quantitative trade signals or alert notifications (owned strictly by `CTX-SIG` / `CTX-ALRT`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Lead Quantitative Technical Analyst  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Active Trader, Quantitative Analyst, Portfolio Manager, Research Analyst  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `TechnicalIndicatorCluster` — Computed technical metrics payload (BDD Sec 8 Service 2 output).  
  - `MomentumSeries` — Time series of calculated momentum indicators.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `MKT-DAT-003` (BCM Domain 1 Market Data — Primary functional execution owner for technical indicator analytics in CTX-TECH).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `RES_TECHNICAL_INDICATOR_COMPUTED` — Triggered when technical indicator calculations complete for a price bar.  
  - `RES_TREND_BREAKOUT_DETECTED` — Triggered when price crosses key moving average or resistance boundary.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `MKT_OHLCV_BAR_AGGREGATED` — Consumed from `CTX-PRC` to trigger technical indicator recalculation.  
  - `MKT_PRICE_TICK_RECEIVED` — Consumed from `CTX-MKT` for intraday real-time indicator updates.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `Technical Indicator`: Mathematical computation derived from price and volume history (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `Momentum`: Rate of acceleration of an instrument's price or volume.  
  - `Support/Resistance`: Price levels where historical buying or selling interest halts price movement.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 18: Technical indicator calculations must satisfy SLA latency boundaries for active trading (BDD Sec 10 Rule 18).  
  - Rule 40: Technical indicator calculations must strictly prohibit look-ahead bias during historical evaluations (BDD Sec 10 Rule 40).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `Technical Indicator` and `Momentum` represent specific mathematical price transformation concepts distinct from `Price` and `Order Block`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 40 (prohibition of look-ahead bias in indicators) applies exclusively here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `RES_TECHNICAL_INDICATOR_COMPUTED` and `RES_TREND_BREAKOUT_DETECTED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `TechnicalIndicatorCluster` and `MomentumSeries` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Indicator calculations execute synchronously on every completed price bar interval.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Lead Quantitative Technical Analyst.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-PRC: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes historical OHLCV price series to compute indicators.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-SCRN: Consumes technical indicator values for multi-variable technical screeners (e.g., RSI < 30).  
  - CTX-SIG: Consumes indicator values to detect quantitative signal setups.  
  - CTX-ALRT: Consumes breakout events to dispatch technical price alert notifications.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Computes technical indicators for all EGX listed equities and indices (EGX30, EGX70, EGX100), accounting for EGX trading session hours and temporary circuit breaker halts.  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:  
  Technical indicators are quantitative mathematical metrics derived from public exchange data and do not constitute licensed investment advice (Principle 3.2).  

CURRENT STATE:  
  Phase 1 (EGX Target)  

FUTURE EVOLUTION:  
  Will expand in Phase 2 to compute multi-timeframe indicators across regional MENA markets and global asset classes in Phase 3.

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Technical indicator calculations MUST NOT utilize future price bar data during historical evaluation (Rule 40).  
    Business Rationale: Eliminates look-ahead bias to ensure mathematically valid historical analysis.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Strict historical boundary check on price bar input parameters.  
    Violation Consequence: Calculation rejection; flags look-ahead error.

    Enforcement Mechanism: Event-driven trigger on `MKT_OHLCV_BAR_AGGREGATED`.  
    Violation Consequence: Stale indicator flag rendered on UI.  
  INV-03: Moving average calculations MUST use a minimum required historical price bar count equal to the period length (e.g., 200 bars for 200-day SMA).  
    Business Rationale: Prevents mathematically corrupted indicator values on insufficient historical data.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Minimum data length validation check.  
    Violation Consequence: Indicator output suppressed as insufficient history.

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-MAC

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Macro Research tracks national and regional macroeconomic indicator series (CPI inflation, Central Bank interest rates, GDP growth, foreign exchange reserves, T-bill yield curves). It provides the macro regime baseline necessary for portfolio risk modeling and asset valuation.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for acquiring, standardizing, and tracking national and international macroeconomic statistical series, Central Bank monetary policy decisions, inflation rate trends, and Treasury yield curve structures across target operating countries.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Tracking macroeconomic statistical indicator series (Consumer Price Index - CPI, inflation %, GDP growth, trade balance, unemployment).  
  - Monitoring Central Bank monetary policy decisions (overnight corridor interest rates, reserve requirements).  
  - Yield curve modeling for national Treasury Bills and Government Bonds (clean/dirty price basis, day-count conventions per Rule 34).  
  - Tracking sovereign credit ratings and country risk premium series.  
  - Macroeconomic indicator observation history management.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Scheduled macroeconomic release event calendars and release alarm timing (owned strictly by `CTX-ECON`).  
  - Dynamic market psychological regime classification like Risk-On / Risk-Off (owned strictly by `CTX-REGIME`).  
  - Corporate financial statement analysis or stock DCF modeling (owned strictly by `CTX-FUND`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Chief Macroeconomic Strategist  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Fund Manager, Wealth Advisor, Portfolio Manager, Research Analyst  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `EconomicIndicator` (BDD Sec 9 Object 13) — Macroeconomic statistical series tracking country-level economic health.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `RES-MAC-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 2) — Economic Indicator Tracking (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `MAC_ECONOMIC_DATA_PUBLISHED` (BDD Sec 12 Event 8) — Triggered when a new macroeconomic indicator observation is released.  
  - `MAC_INTEREST_RATE_CHANGED` — Triggered when a Central Bank announces an interest rate adjustment.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `CAL_SESSION_STARTED` — Consumed to synchronize macro data verification pipelines.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `EconomicIndicator`: Macroeconomic statistical series (e.g., CPI, GDP, Interest Rate) (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `Yield Curve`: Graphical and mathematical representation of interest rates across bond maturities.  
  - `Central Bank`: National monetary authority governing monetary policy and interest rates.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 11: All monetary macroeconomic values must carry explicit ISO currency context (BDD Sec 10 Rule 11).  
  - Rule 12: Cross-currency macroeconomic calculations must use a declared exchange rate source (BDD Sec 10 Rule 12).  
  - Rule 34: Yield calculations on fixed-income instruments must explicitly declare clean vs dirty price basis and day-count conventions (BDD Sec 10 Rule 34).

    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory day-count attribute requirement in yield curve calculation handler.  
    Violation Consequence: Yield model calculation rejection.  
  INV-03: Historical macroeconomic series MUST be immutable once recorded; revisions by statistical agencies MUST be appended as official revision records.  
    Business Rationale: Preserves historical auditability and model backtesting validity.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Append-only persistent data policy.  
    Violation Consequence: Overwrite attempt rejection.

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-QUANT

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Differentiating  
  Justification:     Quantitative Research models cross-sectional factor scores (Value, Quality, Momentum, Size, Low Volatility), sector heatmaps, and strategy backtesting simulations. It enables active traders and fund managers to validate quantitative factor models prior to capital deployment.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for computing multi-factor quantitative scores, building cross-sectional asset rankings, aggregating sector performance heatmaps, and executing historical backtesting simulations for quantitative investment strategies.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Computation of multi-factor scores (`FactorScore`) across Value, Quality, Momentum, Size, and Volatility dimensions.  
  - Building cross-sectional universe percentile rankings for listed instruments.  
  - Aggregating sector performance heatmaps and market-cap weighted sector rotation indicators.  
  - Execution of historical strategy backtesting simulations (`Backtest`) against historical market data (Rule 31).  
  - Backtest performance evaluation metrics (CAGR, Max Drawdown %, Sharpe Ratio, Win Rate %, Trade Drag).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Real-time quote tick ingestion or historical price bar storage (owned strictly by `CTX-MKT` / `CTX-PRC`).  
  - Standard single technical indicator computations like RSI or MACD (owned strictly by `CTX-TECH`).  
  - Synthesis of individual user investment recommendations (owned strictly by `CTX-REC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Quantitative Research & Factor Modeling  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Active Trader, Quantitative Analyst, Fund Manager, Portfolio Manager  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `FactorScore` (BDD Sec 9 Object 38) — Quantitative factor metric evaluating Value, Quality, Momentum, Size.  
  - `Strategy` (BDD Sec 9 Object 27) — Defined quantitative methodology incorporating parameter rules and risk limits.  
  - `Backtest` (BDD Sec 9 Object 28) — Historical simulation evaluation of a Strategy against market history.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `RES-SEC-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 2) — Sector Heatmap Aggregation (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:

CONSUMED EVENTS:

  - `RES_FINANCIAL_STATEMENT_PARSED` — Consumed from `CTX-FUND` to update fundamental factor scores (Value, Quality).  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `FactorScore`: Quantitative metric evaluating an asset across Value, Quality, Momentum, and Size (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `Backtest`: Historical simulation evaluation of a Strategy against historical market data (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `Strategy`: Defined methodology incorporating parameter rules and risk limits (UL Sec 2.1).  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 31: Automated backtesting simulations must account for bid-ask spreads and estimated trading fee drag (BDD Sec 10 Rule 31).  
  - Rule 40: No analytical score or indicator may use future data in historical backtesting calculations (BDD Sec 10 Rule 40).

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Automated backtesting simulations MUST incorporate bid-ask spreads and estimated trading fee drag (Rule 31).  
    Business Rationale: Prevents unrealistic paper profits in historical backtests caused by ignoring real-world transaction friction.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory transaction cost handler in backtesting execution loop.  
    Violation Consequence: Backtest simulation rejection; flags parameter error.  
  INV-02: Factor score evaluations MUST be cross-sectionally normalized across the target instrument universe (e.g., z-score or percentile rank).  
    Business Rationale: Ensures comparable relative factor rankings across diverse market caps and sectors.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Normalization validation filter in factor calculation handler.  
    Violation Consequence: Factor score calculation error.  
  INV-03: Backtesting calculations MUST NOT utilize future data timestamps under any circumstance (Rule 40).  
    Business Rationale: Protects quantitative simulation integrity from catastrophic look-ahead bias.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Strict historical timestamp boundary check.  
    Violation Consequence: Immediate simulation abort; logs rule violation.

It combines fundamental DCF models, quantitative factor scores, and user suitability constraints into zero-hallucination, explainable recommendations, driving Tradeora's AI-first competitive edge.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for synthesizing personalized investment proposals (buy/sell/hold/rebalance), matching proposal parameters against user risk profiles and portfolio constraints, and attaching mandatory suitability disclaimers.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Synthesis of personalized asset recommendation proposals (Buy, Sell, Hold, Rebalance).  
  - Matching recommendation candidate assets against user RiskProfile constraints and investment horizons.  
  - Attaching explicit assumption lists and downside risk warnings to every recommendation (Rule 1).  
  - Recommendation lifecycle management (Active, Pending User Review, Executed, Expired).  
  - Multi-asset recommendation proposal aggregation.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Direct execution of trade orders or brokerage order routing (owned strictly by `CTX-EXEC` per Principle 3.2).  
  - Generating raw technical indicator math or fundamental DCF calculations (owned strictly by `CTX-TECH` / `CTX-FUND`).  
  - Statistical confidence calibration scoring (owned strictly by `CTX-CONF`).

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-CONF

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-CONF  
CANONICAL NAME:      Recommendation Confidence Calibration  
ARABIC NAME:         معايرة الثقة في التوصيات  
CONTEXT CODE:        CONF  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      AI Intelligence Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Differentiating  
  Justification:     Recommendation Confidence Calibration computes statistical uncertainty scores (0.00% to 100.00%) for AI outputs based on historical model accuracy, input data freshness, and market volatility. It prevents user over-reliance on uncertain AI predictions during regime shifts.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for calculating, calibrating, and auditing statistical confidence scores and model uncertainty ratings for all AI recommendations and signals across market volatility regimes.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Computation of statistical confidence percentages (0.00% to 100.00%) for AI recommendations (Rule 1).  
  - Calibration of model uncertainty ratings based on historical prediction accuracy logs.  
  - Data freshness penalty calculations (penalizing confidence when input price or financial data is delayed).  
  - Volatility regime adjustments (reducing confidence during extreme circuit-breaker market spikes).  
  - Historical confidence calibration audit logs.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Generating candidate recommendation trade proposals (owned strictly by `CTX-REC`).  
  - Technical indicator computation or price tick ingestion (owned strictly by `CTX-TECH` / `CTX-PRC`).  
  - Portfolio risk VaR modeling (owned strictly by `CTX-RISK`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Lead AI Model Risk & Validation Officer  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Beginner Investor, Long-Term Investor, Active Trader, System  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `ConfidenceScore` (BDD Sec 9 Object 19 — Calibrated Score Aspect) — Calibrated statistical certainty metric payload.  
  - `UncertaintyMatrix` — Grid evaluating historical model error across volatility regimes.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `AI-REC-002` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 3) — Recommendation Confidence Calibration (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `AI_CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATED` — Triggered when calibrated confidence score is attached to an AI output.  
  - `AI_UNCERTAINTY_FLAGGED` — Triggered when confidence score falls below minimum threshold (< 50%).  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `AI_RECOMMENDATION_GENERATED` — Consumed from `CTX-REC` to evaluate raw recommendation candidate.  
  - `MKT_FEED_STALE_DETECTED` — Consumed from `CTX-MKT` to trigger data freshness confidence penalties.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `ConfidenceScore`: Statistical certainty metric (0.00% to 100.00%) assigned to an AI inference (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `Calibration`: Process of adjusting model certainty scores to align with empirical historical accuracy.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 1: All AI outputs must explicitly state confidence score percentage (0.00% to 100.00%) (BDD Sec 10 Rule 1).  
  - Rule 7: Data freshness degradation must penalize AI confidence ratings automatically (BDD Sec 10 Rule 7).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `ConfidenceScore` and `UncertaintyMatrix` represent statistical validation concepts distinct from `Recommendation` and `RiskProfile`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 1 (mandatory 0-100% score display) and Rule 7 (freshness penalty) apply explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `AI_CONFIDENCE_CALIBRATED` and `AI_UNCERTAINTY_FLAGGED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of calibrated `ConfidenceScore` and `UncertaintyMatrix` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Confidence scores are dynamically recalibrated post-inference as market data age increases.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Lead AI Model Risk & Validation Officer.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-REC: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes recommendation candidates for confidence scoring.  
  - CTX-MKT: Customer/Supplier | SOFT | Consumes data feed freshness metrics.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-REC: Consumes calibrated confidence scores to filter out low-confidence proposals (< 60%).  
  - CTX-ASSIST: Consumes confidence metrics to disclose AI uncertainty during conversational dialogue.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Adjusts confidence scores based on EGX market data freshness, trading session state, and stock liquidity tiers (e.g., lower confidence assigned to low-liquidity Nilex equities).  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:  
  Fulfills regulatory transparency requirements by explicitly warning users when AI confidence is degraded by market volatility or stale data.  

CURRENT STATE:  
  Phase 1 (EGX Target)  

FUTURE EVOLUTION:  
  Will expand in Phase 2 to incorporate Bayesian uncertainty calibration models and real-time ensemble model variance scoring in Phase 3.

  INV-01: Every AI output MUST display a calibrated ConfidenceScore percentage formatted between 0.00% and 100.00% (Rule 1).

    Violation Consequence: Confidence score recalculation forced.

    Enforcement Mechanism: Minimum threshold filter in recommendation dispatch pipeline.  
    Violation Consequence: Proposal suppressed; flags low confidence log.

  - Construction of structured Abstract Syntax Trees (`ParsedQueryAST`).

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-RAG

ARABIC NAME:         استرجاع وتوليد المعرفة المالية

  Justification:     Enterprise RAG System manages vector embeddings, semantic document chunking, and context retrieval across structured financial statements, research reports, and market news. It provides the grounded context payload enforcing Tradeora's zero-hallucination mandate.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for indexing financial document knowledge bases into dense vector embeddings (`KnowledgeEmbeddings`), executing semantic similarity retrieval, and building grounded context payloads (`RetrievedContext`) for downstream AI engines.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Vector embedding generation and management (`KnowledgeEmbeddings`) for financial documents.  
  - Semantic document chunking (`VectorChunk`) for financial disclosures, research reports, and news.  
  - Hybrid dense/sparse semantic retrieval and vector similarity search.  
  - Construction of grounded context payloads (`RetrievedContext`) with explicit document source citations (Rule 7).  
  - Knowledge base index synchronization and document embedding lifecycle management.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Raw financial news media ingestion or news sentiment scoring (owned strictly by `CTX-SENT`).  
  - Extracting or standardizing raw PDF balance sheet tables (owned strictly by `CTX-FUND`).  
  - Managing user conversational chat sessions or rendering text responses (owned strictly by `CTX-ASSIST`).

  Lead Vector Data Architecture & RAG Systems Architect

  System, AI Recommendation Engine, Conversational AI Assistant, Research Analyst

  - `VectorChunk` — Standardized semantic text passage chunk with embedding vector.  
  - `KnowledgeEmbeddings` — Dense vector index catalog representing enterprise knowledge base.  
  - `RetrievedContext` — Grounded passage payload retrieved to ground an AI inference.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `AI-RES-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 3 — Knowledge Base Context Retrieval Aspect — Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `AI_KNOWLEDGE_RETRIEVED` — Triggered when grounded context passages are retrieved for a query.

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `VectorChunk`: Semantic text passage chunk paired with dense embedding vector.  
  - `GroundedContext`: Verified document evidence payload forcing zero-hallucination AI generation.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-PORT

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-PORT  
CANONICAL NAME:      Portfolio Tracking & NAV  
ARABIC NAME:         متابعة المحافظ وقيمة الأصول  
CONTEXT CODE:        PORT  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Portfolio Management Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Portfolio Tracking & NAV aggregates user asset holdings, cash balances, and real-time market prices into an authoritative Net Asset Value (NAV) valuation snapshot. It provides the core financial accounting baseline for total portfolio monitoring.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for aggregating position quantities and cash balances into total Net Asset Value (NAV) snapshots, computing unrealized P&L, and maintaining portfolio baseline valuation ledgers.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Aggregation of portfolio total Net Asset Value (NAV) snapshots across multi-asset holdings.  
  - Computation of real-time unrealized P&L figures based on current market price streams.  
  - Maintenance of user Portfolio aggregate containers (`Portfolio`).  
  - Valuation currency baseline conversion into declared base accounting currency (EGP baseline).  
  - Portfolio valuation snapshot history preservation.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Individual asset position share ledgers or execution trade lot accounting (owned strictly by `CTX-POS` / `CTX-TAX`).  
  - Time-Weighted Return (TWR) performance attribution or benchmark comparison (owned strictly by `CTX-PERF`).  
  - Trade execution routing or broker order staging (owned strictly by `CTX-EXEC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Portfolio Accounting & Asset Valuation  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Beginner Investor, Long-Term Investor, Active Trader, Portfolio Manager, Wealth Advisor  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `Portfolio` (BDD Sec 9 Object 21) — User portfolio container managing total asset allocation and NAV valuation.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `PRT-TRK-001` (Scoped Shared Kernel — Primary NAV aggregation & portfolio valuation owner in CTX-PORT; position share quantity ledger aspect owned by CTX-POS. Registered in Appendix A).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `PORT_VALUATION_COMPUTED` — Triggered when a new real-time NAV valuation snapshot is computed.  
  - `PORT_NAV_UPDATED` — Triggered when total portfolio Net Asset Value changes significantly.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `PORT_POSITION_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-POS` when underlying position quantity changes.  
  - `MKT_EOD_PRICES_PUBLISHED` — Consumed from `CTX-PRC` to execute daily post-session NAV valuation close.

    Object difference: OWNS `Portfolio`; does NOT own `PerformanceSeries` or `AttributionMatrix`.  
    Event difference: Produces `PORT_VALUATION_COMPUTED`; does NOT produce `PERF_RETURN_COMPUTED`.

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Portfolio Net Asset Value (NAV) MUST strictly satisfy the fundamental valuation equation: `Portfolio NAV = Σ (Position Quantities × Current Market Prices) + Cash Balances` (Rule 5 & BDD Policy 21).  
    Business Rationale: Guarantees 100% mathematical precision and financial accounting integrity across portfolio views.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory valuation balance equation check on every NAV snapshot calculation.  
    Violation Consequence: NAV snapshot rejected; flags calculation discrepancy log.  
  INV-02: Every Portfolio NAV calculation MUST be expressed in a declared Base Accounting Currency (`EGP` for baseline), converting non-base currency assets using authoritative spot exchange rates (Rule 11).  
    Business Rationale: Ensures consistent currency baseline for portfolio monitoring and risk evaluation.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory base currency parameter check on Portfolio entity.  
    Violation Consequence: Multi-currency NAV calculation aborted.  
  INV-03: Assets lacking a verified current market price MUST be flagged as `UNPRICED_ASSET` and excluded from real-time unrealized P&L calculations (Rule 5).  
    Business Rationale: Prevents stale or inaccurate pricing from corrupting total portfolio NAV.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Pricing verification filter in NAV calculation pipeline.  
    Violation Consequence: Asset marked unpriced; warning rendered on UI.

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-POS

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-POS  
CANONICAL NAME:      Position Ledger & Accounting  
ARABIC NAME:         سجل المراكز والمحاسبة  
CONTEXT CODE:        POS  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Portfolio Management Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Position Ledger & Accounting maintains the authoritative legal share quantity ledger (`Position`) for all asset holdings within user portfolios. It tracks share balances, corporate action adjustments, and average cost bases across trade execution events.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for maintaining authoritative position share quantity ledgers, processing position adjustments from trade execution fills and corporate actions, and calculating weighted average cost bases.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Maintenance of authoritative asset position share quantity ledgers (`Position`).  
  - Position quantity updates triggered by trade execution fills (Buy, Sell, Short).  
  - Position adjustments resulting from corporate actions (stock splits, bonus shares, reverse splits per Rule 9).  
  - Calculation of weighted average cost basis per share position.  
  - Position lifecycle tracking (Opened, Active, Reduced, Closed).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Aggregate portfolio total Net Asset Value (NAV) calculation (owned strictly by `CTX-PORT`).  
  - Individual purchase tax lot breakdown (FIFO/LIFO) for tax reporting (owned strictly by `CTX-TAX`).  
  - Direct execution of trade orders on exchange (owned strictly by `CTX-EXEC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Position Accounting & Ledger Operations  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Portfolio Manager, Active Trader, Individual Investor, Compliance Officer  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `Position` (BDD Sec 9 Object 22) — Authoritative asset position record detailing share quantity and cost basis.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `PRT-TRK-001` (Scoped Shared Kernel — Primary position share quantity ledger owner in CTX-POS; NAV aggregation & portfolio valuation aspect owned by CTX-PORT. Registered in Appendix A).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `PORT_POSITION_CREATED` — Triggered when a new asset position is opened in a portfolio.  
  - `PORT_POSITION_UPDATED` — Triggered when position quantity or cost basis is modified.  
  - `PORT_POSITION_CLOSED` — Triggered when a position share quantity reaches zero.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `EXEC_ORDER_FILLED` — Consumed from `CTX-EXEC` to update position quantity following trade execution.  
  - `CORP_SPLIT_EFFECTED` — Consumed from `CTX-CORP` to adjust position share counts for stock splits.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `Position`: Authoritative asset record detailing share quantity, cost basis, and holding state (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `CostBasis`: Total purchase cost allocated per share held in a position.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 9: Corporate action events (splits, bonus shares) must reflect in position holdings within 1 business day (BDD Sec 10 Rule 9).  
  - Rule 35: Position cost basis accounting must preserve original trade execution currency context (BDD Sec 10 Rule 35).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `Position` and `CostBasis` represent transactional share accounting concepts distinct from `Portfolio` and `TaxLot`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 9 (corporate action position reflection) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `PORT_POSITION_CREATED`, `PORT_POSITION_UPDATED`, and `PORT_POSITION_CLOSED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `Position` object ledger.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Positions update on transactional trade settlement and corporate action events independently of real-time price tick streams.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Position Accounting & Ledger Operations.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-SEC: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes Instrument metadata.  
  - CTX-EXEC: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes trade execution receipts.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-PORT: Consumes position quantities to compute total portfolio Net Asset Value (NAV).  
  - CTX-TAX: Consumes position quantity updates to create detailed tax lots.  
  - CTX-RISK: Consumes position holdings for sector concentration and risk stress-testing.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Tracks position share quantities for EGX listed equities, Nilex SME stocks, and Egyptian sovereign bonds, adjusting for T+2 settlement cycles and EGX corporate action rules.  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:

    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory dual-currency cost basis check on Position entity.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for calculating GIPS-compliant Time-Weighted Returns (TWR), evaluating benchmark alpha generation, and modeling asset allocation performance attribution across historical reporting periods.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:

  - Evaluation of benchmark comparison metrics (Alpha, Beta, Tracking Error, Sharpe Ratio, Information Ratio).  
  - Sector and asset allocation performance attribution modeling (Brinson attribution model).  
  - Maintenance of portfolio performance time series (`PerformanceSeries`).  
  - Management of benchmark index return series (`Benchmark`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Instantaneous portfolio Net Asset Value (NAV) market calculation (owned strictly by `CTX-PORT`).

OWNED CAPABILITIES:

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Tracking foreign exchange spot rate series (`ExchangeRate`) across target currency pairs (USD/EGP, EUR/EGP, SAR/EGP).  
  - Managing currency definitions (`Currency`) and ISO 4217 code registries.  
  - Executing multi-currency valuation conversion calculations (Rule 11 & Rule 12).  
  - Calculating realized and unrealized foreign exchange gain/loss metrics for multi-market portfolios.  
  - Foreign exchange spot rate history management.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Macroeconomic interest rate curve modeling or national inflation statistics (owned strictly by `CTX-MAC`).  
  - Individual asset position share quantity ledgers (owned strictly by `CTX-POS`).

  - Ordering and presentation layout preferences for watchlist items.  
  - User watchlist storage management.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Actual capital position share quantity accounting or portfolio NAV tracking (owned strictly by `CTX-POS` / `CTX-PORT`).

  - Price alert threshold triggering or push notification dispatches (owned strictly by `CTX-ALRT`).

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-PORT (Portfolio NAV):  
    Language difference: `Watchlist` is a prospective monitoring preference; `Portfolio` is an active capital position container.  
    Rule difference: Rule 7 (source attribution for watchlist items) vs Rule 5 (pricing valuation for capital NAV).  
    Object difference: OWNS `Watchlist`; does NOT own `Portfolio` or `Position`.  
    Event difference: Produces `WATCHLIST_CREATED`; does NOT produce `PORT_NAV_UPDATED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-WATCH` operates on user UI editing cadences (zero capital value) independently of market trading sessions; `CTX-PORT` recalculates real-time capital valuations on every price tick stream update.  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-SCRN (Screener Engine):  
    Language difference: `Watchlist` is a static user-curated collection of instruments; `ScreeningQuery` is a dynamic multi-variable filtering rule.  
    Rule difference: Watchlist item management rules vs screener multi-variable execution rules.  
    Object difference: OWNS `Watchlist`; does NOT own `ScreeningQuery` or `ScreeningResult`.  
    Event difference: Produces `WATCHLIST_INSTRUMENT_ADDED`; does NOT produce `SCREENER_QUERY_EXECUTED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-WATCH` maintains static persistent list records; `CTX-SCRN` executes real-time dynamic query evaluation against market databases.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Watchlists MUST contain valid listed instruments exclusively; deleted or delisted instruments MUST be automatically archived or flagged (Rule 7).  
    Business Rationale: Prevents stale or invalid ticker symbols from cluttering user watchlists.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Instrument validity check on `INST_SECURITY_DELISTED` event receipt.  
    Violation Consequence: Delisted instrument flagged on watchlist UI.  
  INV-02: Maximum item count per watchlist MUST enforce user subscription tier boundaries (e.g., max 50 instruments for Free Tier, unlimited for Pro).  
    Business Rationale: Protects UI rendering performance and supports tier monetization.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Item count limit check on watchlist item insertion.  
    Violation Consequence: Addition rejected; prompts tier upgrade.  
  INV-03: Watchlist item order preferences MUST be preserved across user sessions.  
    Business Rationale: Ensures consistent personalized user experience.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Persistent ordering position index on Watchlist entity.  
    Violation Consequence: Layout reset to default alphabetical order.

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-SCRN  
CANONICAL NAME:      Dynamic Multi-Variable Screener  
ARABIC NAME:         محرك التصفية والفرز

VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Dynamic Multi-Variable Screener executes complex filtering queries across the entire market universe, combining fundamental ratios (P/E, ROE), technical indicators (RSI, Moving Averages), sector classifications, and AI confidence scores into actionable opportunity tables.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for parsing screening criteria rules, executing dynamic multi-variable filtering across asset universes, and returning sorted, paginated screening result tables (`ScreeningResult`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Execution of dynamic multi-variable screening queries across broad asset universes.  
  - Combining fundamental ratios (P/E, P/B, Dividend Yield), technical parameters (RSI, MACD), sector filters, and AI scores in unified query rules.  
  - Managing saved screener query presets (`ScreeningQuery`).  
  - Screening result pagination, sorting, and export generation (`ScreeningResult`).  
  - Pre-computed screening index acceleration management.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Primary computation of fundamental ratios or DCF models (owned strictly by `CTX-FUND`).  
  - Primary computation of technical indicators like RSI or MACD (owned strictly by `CTX-TECH`).  
  - Managing static user-curated asset lists (owned strictly by `CTX-WATCH`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Lead Quantitative Screener & Market Discovery Architect  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Active Trader, Long-Term Investor, Research Analyst, Portfolio Manager  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `ScreeningQuery` — Defined multi-variable filtering query rule payload.  
  - `ScreeningResult` — Filtered, sorted, and paginated instrument result table.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `PRT-WTC-002` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 4) — Dynamic Multi-Variable Screening (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `SCREENER_QUERY_EXECUTED` — Triggered when a multi-variable screening query executes.  
  - `SCREENER_PRESET_SAVED` — Triggered when a user saves a screening query configuration preset.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - User screener query submission actions.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `ScreeningQuery`: Defined multi-variable filtering rule combining fundamental, technical, and AI parameters (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `Universe`: Broad collection of listed financial instruments evaluated by a screener query.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 15: Screener fundamental ratio filters must adhere strictly to standardized IFRS/EAS calculation rules (BDD Sec 10 Rule 15).  
  - Rule 40: Screener query evaluation must strictly disallow look-ahead bias on historical metrics (BDD Sec 10 Rule 40).

  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `ScreeningQuery` and `ScreeningResult` objects.

    Enforcement Mechanism: Database index optimization and query timeout monitoring.  
    Violation Consequence: Query execution fallback to cached result set.

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-TAX

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-TAX  
CANONICAL NAME:      Tax Lot & Cost-Basis Accounting  
ARABIC NAME:         محاسبة الوعاء الضريبي والصفقات  
CONTEXT CODE:        TAX  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Portfolio Management Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Tax Lot & Cost-Basis Accounting tracks individual purchase tax lots (`TaxLot`), trade transaction histories (`HistoricalTrade`), cost-basis accounting methods (FIFO/LIFO/Weighted Average), and realized capital gains/losses for tax audit reporting.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for creating and tracking individual purchase tax lots (`TaxLot`), preserving immutable historical trade logs (`HistoricalTrade`), allocating sold shares to tax lots under FIFO/LIFO rules, and calculating realized capital gains for tax reporting.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Creation and lifecycle tracking of individual purchase tax lots (`TaxLot`).  
  - Preservation of immutable historical trade transaction logs (`HistoricalTrade`).  
  - Tax lot accounting allocation methodologies (First-In First-Out - FIFO, Last-In First-Out - LIFO, Specific Identification).  
  - Computation of realized capital gains and losses upon asset sale events.  
  - Preserving local tax reporting currency cost basis records (EGP baseline per Rule 35).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Aggregate real-time portfolio Net Asset Value (NAV) valuation (owned strictly by `CTX-PORT`).  
  - Aggregate position share balance ledgers (owned strictly by `CTX-POS`).  
  - Execution of brokerage trade orders (owned strictly by `CTX-EXEC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Tax Accounting & Regulatory Compliance  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Portfolio Manager, Individual Investor, Compliance Officer, Tax Auditor  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `TaxLot` — Individual purchase tranche detailing purchase date, quantity, cost basis, and tax status.  
  - `HistoricalTrade` (BDD Sec 9 Object 23) — Immutable historical trade entry detailing buy/sell execution parameters.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `PRT-TRK-002` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 4) — Historical Transaction Recording (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `TAX_LOT_CREATED` — Triggered when a new purchase tax lot is established following trade fill.  
  - `TAX_REALIZED_GAIN_CALCULATED` — Triggered when an asset sale closes tax lots and calculates realized gain/loss.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `EXEC_ORDER_FILLED` — Consumed from `CTX-EXEC` to record historical trade and establish tax lot.  
  - `PORT_POSITION_CLOSED` — Consumed from `CTX-POS` to finalize tax lot realization.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `TaxLot`: Individual purchase tranche tracking purchase date, share count, and cost basis (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `RealizedGain`: Capital gain or loss locked in upon selling a tax lot.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 24: Historical trade records and tax lot logs must be tamper-evident and audit-preserved (BDD Sec 10 Rule 24).  
  - Rule 35: Tax lot cost basis records must preserve original trade execution currency context alongside local tax reporting currency (BDD Sec 10 Rule 35).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `TaxLot` and `RealizedGain` represent tax accounting concepts distinct from `Position` and `Portfolio`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 24 (tamper-evident audit logging for tax records) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `TAX_LOT_CREATED` and `TAX_REALIZED_GAIN_CALCULATED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `TaxLot` and `HistoricalTrade` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Tax lots are created upon purchase and realized upon sale, preserved permanently for multi-year tax audits.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Tax Accounting & Regulatory Compliance.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-POS: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes position updates for tax lot allocation.  
  - CTX-EXEC: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes trade execution confirmation receipts.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-AUDIT: Consumes immutable historical trade logs for regulatory audit reporting.  
  - CTX-UI: Consumes tax lot reports for rendering annual tax statement summaries.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Logs Egyptian capital gains tax calculations, EGX stamp duty tax charges, brokerage commissions, and Egyptian tax authority cost-basis reporting rules.  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:  
  Strict compliance with Egyptian Tax Authority guidelines and Rule 24 (tamper-evident historical trade logging for multi-year tax audits).  

CURRENT STATE:  
  Phase 1 (EGX Target)  

FUTURE EVOLUTION:

  Why this is NOT part of CTX-POS (Position Ledger):  
    Language difference: `TaxLot` is an individual purchase tranche (Lot #1: 200 shares at 80 EGP); `Position` is aggregate share balance (500 shares).  
    Rule difference: Rule 24 (tamper-evident tax log auditability) vs Rule 9 (position share adjustments).  
    Object difference: OWNS `TaxLot` and `HistoricalTrade`; does NOT own `Position`.  
    Event difference: Produces `TAX_REALIZED_GAIN_CALCULATED`; does NOT produce `PORT_POSITION_UPDATED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-POS` updates active share balances instantly upon trade fill; `CTX-TAX` processes tax lot cost-basis allocations and realized gains preserved for multi-year tax audit reporting.  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-PORT (Portfolio NAV):  
    Language difference: `RealizedGain` is locked-in profit/loss upon sale; `NetAssetValue` is real-time paper market valuation.  
    Rule difference: Tax accounting rules vs Rule 5 (pricing valuation).  
    Object difference: OWNS `TaxLot`; does NOT own `Portfolio`.  
    Event difference: Produces `TAX_LOT_CREATED`; does NOT produce `PORT_NAV_UPDATED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-PORT` tracks real-time paper valuation on price tick updates; `CTX-TAX` tracks realized tax gains and historical cost-basis accounting logs preserved for multi-year regulatory tax audits.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: HistoricalTrade records MUST be immutable once committed, enforcing tamper-evident auditability (Rule 24).  
    Business Rationale: Ensures regulatory compliance and prevents tax record tampering.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Append-only cryptographic hash chain policy on HistoricalTrade entity.  
    Violation Consequence: Trade log modification rejected; flags security alert.  
  INV-02: TaxLot cost basis accounting MUST preserve original trade execution currency alongside local tax reporting currency equivalents (Rule 35).  
    Business Rationale: Guarantees accurate tax calculation across multi-currency investments.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Dual-currency cost basis attribute check on TaxLot creation.  
    Violation Consequence: Tax lot creation rejected.  
  INV-03: Realized capital gain calculations upon asset sale MUST follow declared tax lot matching methodology (FIFO baseline) strictly.  
    Business Rationale: Ensures mathematical precision in capital gains tax reporting.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated FIFO lot matching algorithm check.  
    Violation Consequence: Realized gain calculation error.

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-RISK

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-RISK  
CANONICAL NAME:      Portfolio Risk & Stress Testing  
ARABIC NAME:         إدارة المخاطر واختبارات الضغط  
CONTEXT CODE:        RISK  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Risk and Compliance Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Differentiating  
  Justification:     Portfolio Risk & Stress Testing calculates quantitative Value-at-Risk (VaR), Conditional VaR (Expected Shortfall), sector concentration matrices, asset correlations, and historical drawdown stress testing across multi-asset holdings. It provides the central quantitative risk engine protecting investors against tail risk.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for quantifying potential downside loss exposure, capturing user risk tolerance profiles (`RiskProfile`), modeling parametric and historical VaR (`VaRModel`), executing drawdown stress tests under adverse market regimes (`StressScenario`), and evaluating correlation heatmaps.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Calculation of historical, parametric, and Monte Carlo Value-at-Risk (VaR) metrics for user portfolios.  
  - Computation of Conditional VaR (Expected Shortfall) at 95% and 99% confidence horizons.  
  - Sector concentration percentage tracking and asset price correlation matrix computation.  
  - Execution of historical market crash stress-testing simulations (e.g., 2008 global financial crisis, 2020 crash, currency devaluation shocks).  
  - Management of user investment risk profiles (`RiskProfile`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Direct pre-trade order compliance blocking or regulatory entitlement checks (owned strictly by `CTX-COMP`).  
  - Immutable historical audit logging of system events (owned strictly by `CTX-AUD`).  
  - Real-time portfolio Net Asset Value (NAV) market valuation (owned strictly by `CTX-PORT`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Chief Risk Officer (CRO) & Lead Quantitative Risk Architect  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Portfolio Manager, Fund Manager, Wealth Advisor, Active Trader, Individual Investor  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `RiskProfile` (BDD Sec 9 Object 20) — User risk capacity, loss tolerance, and asset allocation constraint parameters.  
  - `VaRModel` — Quantitative model payload containing VaR, Expected Shortfall, and confidence level parameters.  
  - `StressScenario` — Historical market shock simulation payload defining price asset drops and macroeconomic stress regimes.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `RSK-ANL-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 5) — Value-at-Risk (VaR) Modeling (Primary Owner).  
  - `RSK-ANL-002` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 5) — Sector Concentration Risk Stress-Testing (Primary Owner).  
  - `RSK-ANL-003` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 5) — Drawdown Stress-Testing (Primary Owner).  
  - `RSK-PRF-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 5) — User Risk Tolerance Profiling (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `RISK_VAR_COMPUTED` — Triggered when a new portfolio VaR metric is calculated.  
  - `RISK_CONCENTRATION_BREACHED` — Triggered when portfolio sector or single-stock concentration exceeds risk limit.  
  - `RISK_STRESS_TEST_COMPLETED` — Triggered when a drawdown stress test scenario simulation finishes.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `PORT_NAV_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-PORT` to trigger risk model recalculation.  
  - `PORT_POSITION_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-POS` to update risk asset weights.  
  - `MKT_EOD_PRICES_PUBLISHED` — Consumed from `CTX-PRC` to update asset volatility series.  
  - `MAC_ECONOMIC_DATA_PUBLISHED` — Consumed from `CTX-MAC` to calibrate stress scenario shock vectors.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `ValueAtRisk`: Maximum expected monetary loss over a time horizon at a specified confidence level (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `ExpectedShortfall`: Expected monetary loss given that the loss exceeds the VaR threshold (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `ConcentrationRisk`: Risk of financial loss arising from over-exposure to a single asset or business sector.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 20: Quantitative risk metrics (VaR, Expected Shortfall) must use verified statistical distribution models and minimum 250-trading-day historical price series (BDD Sec 10 Rule 20).  
  - Rule 21: Concentration risk warning thresholds must be enforced for single-stock holdings exceeding declared portfolio limits (BDD Sec 10 Rule 21).  
  - Rule 34: Stress-testing models must incorporate macro currency devaluation and volatility regime shifts (BDD Sec 10 Rule 34).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `ValueAtRisk`, `ExpectedShortfall`, and `StressScenario` represent quantitative risk concepts distinct from `NetAssetValue` and `TimeWeightedReturn`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 20 (statistical distribution and 250-day window for VaR) applies explicitly here.

  Why this is NOT part of CTX-PORT (Portfolio NAV):  
    Language difference: `ValueAtRisk` / `ExpectedShortfall` is a statistical prospective downside loss distribution; `NetAssetValue` is an instantaneous paper market valuation snapshot.  
    Rule difference: Rule 20 (250-day historical window for VaR) vs Rule 5 (pricing valuation for NAV).  
    Object difference: OWNS `RiskProfile` and `VaRModel`; does NOT own `Portfolio`.  
    Event difference: Produces `RISK_VAR_COMPUTED`; does NOT produce `PORT_NAV_UPDATED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-PORT` evaluates real-time paper NAV valuations on price tick arrival (sub-second cycle); `CTX-RISK` projects prospective future downside loss scenarios (VaR, stress tests) across 250-day statistical simulation windows.  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-PERF (Performance Attribution):  
    Language difference: `ValueAtRisk` projects prospective future downside loss exposure; `TimeWeightedReturn` measures past historical return skill.  
    Rule difference: Rule 20 (VaR statistical modeling) vs GIPS performance return rules.  
    Object difference: OWNS `VaRModel` and `StressScenario`; does NOT own `PerformanceSeries` or `Benchmark`.  
    Event difference: Produces `RISK_STRESS_TEST_COMPLETED`; does NOT produce `PERF_RETURN_COMPUTED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-PERF` measures past historical return logs over daily/monthly reporting horizons; `CTX-RISK` projects prospective future loss distributions across statistical volatility windows.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Value-at-Risk (VaR) calculations MUST utilize a minimum 250-trading-day historical price observation window (or equivalent Monte Carlo simulation parameters) at 95% and 99% confidence levels (Rule 20).  
    Business Rationale: Ensures statistical validity and prevents sample size underfitting in tail-risk estimation.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory historical window length validation check in VaR calculation pipeline.  
    Violation Consequence: VaR calculation rejected; returns insufficient data error.  
  INV-02: Single-stock concentration risk limit MUST never exceed 20% of total portfolio Net Asset Value (NAV) (or explicit user-defined RiskProfile limit), triggering an immediate `RISK_CONCENTRATION_BREACHED` event (Rule 21).  
    Business Rationale: Protects investors against catastrophic single-issuer default risk.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated concentration ratio validator on portfolio position update.  
    Violation Consequence: Breach event dispatched; concentration warning flagged on UI.  
  INV-03: Stress-testing simulations MUST incorporate macro currency devaluation shocks and historical volatility regime shift vectors (Rule 34).  
    Business Rationale: Prepares portfolios for severe tail-risk events and currency devaluation shocks.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory macroeconomic shock parameter check on StressScenario execution.  
    Violation Consequence: Stress test simulation aborted.

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Investment Compliance & Limits provides prospective real-time and pre-trade enforcement of regulatory investment mandates, user risk profile constraints, margin policy limits, and single-stock concentration rules. It prevents non-compliant trade orders from reaching execution venues.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for evaluating pre-trade order parameters against investment rules (`ComplianceRule`), detecting potential policy breaches before execution, and maintaining compliance breach records (`BreachRecord`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Real-time prospective and pre-trade compliance rule evaluation (`ComplianceRule`).  
  - Pre-trade blocking of orders violating single-stock concentration limits (20% cap per Rule 21) or regulatory restrictions.  
  - Enforcement of investor suitability constraints based on user `RiskProfile` metrics.  
  - Management of active compliance breach records (`BreachRecord`).  
  - Pre-trade compliance pass/fail validation tokens.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Permanent retrospective immutable audit logging of past system events (owned strictly by `CTX-AUD`).  
  - Quantitative Value-at-Risk (VaR) calculation or drawdown stress testing (owned strictly by `CTX-RISK`).  
  - Direct execution routing of trade orders to stock exchanges (owned strictly by `CTX-EXEC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) & Legal Regulatory Director  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Compliance Officer, Portfolio Manager, Risk Evaluator, Individual Investor  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `ComplianceRule` — Defined compliance validation rule payload (e.g., max 20% single-stock cap, restricted list ticker block).  
  - `BreachRecord` — Record detailing prospective compliance rule breach event parameters.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `ENG-ALT-002` (Scoped Shared Kernel — Primary prospective compliance breach enforcement owner in CTX-COMP; user alert dispatch aspect owned by CTX-ALRT. Registered in Appendix A).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `COMP_RULE_EVALUATED` — Triggered when a pre-trade or real-time compliance validation check completes.  
  - `COMP_BREACH_DETECTED` — Triggered when a compliance rule violation blocks an order or flags a portfolio.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `RISK_CONCENTRATION_BREACHED` — Consumed from `CTX-RISK` to trigger prospective compliance warning blocks.  
  - `PORT_POSITION_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-POS` to re-evaluate active portfolio compliance limits.  
  - `EXEC_ORDER_STAGED` — Consumed from `CTX-EXEC` to execute mandatory pre-trade compliance evaluation.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `ComplianceRule`: Prospective policy constraint governing permissible trading actions and holdings (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `BreachRecord`: Formal record documenting an attempted or active violation of compliance constraints.  
  - `PreTradeValidation`: Synchronous evaluation of trade orders against compliance rules prior to broker transmission.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:

  - Rule 3.2: Compliance engine operates in non-custodial decision support mode; mandatory human confirmation is required for all trade execution overrides (BDD Sec 10 Rule 3.2 & Constitution Principle 3.2).
