  Why this is NOT part of CTX-AUD (Audit Trail & Regulatory Reporting):  
    Prospective Rules vs Retrospective Records Distinction:  
      `CTX-COMP` (Compliance) operates PROSPECTIVELY in real-time or pre-trade mode to evaluate active investment policy rules, single-stock caps (20%), and suitability constraints BEFORE or DURING execution to PREVENT breaches.  
      `CTX-AUD` (Audit) operates RETROSPECTIVELY to record permanent, immutable post-trade audit logs (`AuditLog`) of actions that ALREADY occurred for multi-year regulatory verification and non-repudiation.  
    Language difference: `ComplianceRule` is an active prospective constraint; `AuditLog` is a retrospective immutable record entry.  
    Rule difference: Rule 3.2 (non-custodial pre-trade decision support) vs Rule 24 (tamper-evident historical audit preservation).  
    Object difference: OWNS `ComplianceRule` and `BreachRecord`; does NOT own `AuditLog` or `RegulatoryReport`.  
    Event difference: Produces `COMP_RULE_EVALUATED`; does NOT produce `AUDIT_EVENT_LOGGED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-COMP` operates on sub-50ms pre-trade execution evaluation cadences; `CTX-AUD` operates on permanent append-only historical archiving cadences.  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-RISK (Risk Management):  
    Language difference: `ComplianceRule` is a pass/fail legal policy rule; `ValueAtRisk` is a continuous quantitative statistical loss metric.  
    Rule difference: Rule 1 (pre-trade risk warnings & assumptions) vs Rule 20 (250-day VaR statistical window).  
    Object difference: OWNS `ComplianceRule`; does NOT own `VaRModel` or `StressScenario`.  
    Event difference: Produces `COMP_BREACH_DETECTED`; does NOT produce `RISK_VAR_COMPUTED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-COMP` executes instant pass/fail validation on staged orders; `CTX-RISK` executes quantitative matrix calculations across historical volatility series.

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for capturing append-only immutable audit event streams (`AuditLog`), enforcing non-repudiation provenance chains, and compiling regulatory disclosure reports (`RegulatoryReport`) in compliance with FRA mandates and Constitution Principle 4.40.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:

  - Cryptographic tamper-evident hash chain verification for audit records.  
  - Compilation of official regulatory disclosure reports (`RegulatoryReport`) for financial regulators.  
  - Non-repudiation provenance tracking linking user actions, AI recommendations, and timestamps.  
  - Multi-year regulatory audit log data retention management.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Prospective real-time pre-trade compliance rule evaluation or order blocking (owned strictly by `CTX-COMP`).  
  - Quantitative Value-at-Risk (VaR) statistical loss modeling (owned strictly by `CTX-RISK`).

  - `RegulatoryReport` — Official regulatory compliance disclosure report compiled for financial regulatory authorities.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `OPS-GOV-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 10) — Immutable Audit Event Logging (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `AUDIT_EVENT_LOGGED` — Triggered when a new immutable audit record is committed to the hash chain.  
  - `AUDIT_REPORT_GENERATED` — Triggered when an official regulatory disclosure report is compiled.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-COMP (Investment Compliance):  
    Retrospective Records vs Prospective Rules Distinction:  
      `CTX-AUD` (Audit) operates RETROSPECTIVELY to record permanent, immutable post-trade audit logs (`AuditLog`) of actions that ALREADY occurred for multi-year regulatory verification and non-repudiation.  
      `CTX-COMP` (Compliance) operates PROSPECTIVELY in real-time or pre-trade mode to evaluate active investment policy rules, single-stock caps (20%), and suitability constraints BEFORE or DURING execution to PREVENT breaches.  
    Language difference: `AuditLog` is a retrospective immutable record entry; `ComplianceRule` is an active prospective constraint.  
    Rule difference: Rule 24 (tamper-evident historical audit preservation) vs Rule 3.2 (non-custodial pre-trade decision support).  
    Object difference: OWNS `AuditLog` and `RegulatoryReport`; does NOT own `ComplianceRule` or `BreachRecord`.  
    Event difference: Produces `AUDIT_EVENT_LOGGED`; does NOT produce `COMP_RULE_EVALUATED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-AUD` operates on permanent append-only historical archiving cadences; `CTX-COMP` operates on sub-50ms pre-trade execution evaluation cadences.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: AuditLog records MUST be immutable once committed, protected by cryptographic append-only hash chain validation (Principle 4.40 & Rule 3 & Rule 24).  
    Business Rationale: Ensures absolute legal non-repudiation and prevents audit record tampering.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory SHA-256 append-only hash validation on AuditLog insertion.  
    Violation Consequence: Insertion rejected; flags tamper attempt security alert.  
  INV-02: Regulatory report compilations MUST preserve complete non-repudiation provenance linking user actions, AI inference payloads, and market timestamps (Rule 3).  
    Business Rationale: Guarantees complete auditability for regulatory supervisory reviews.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory correlation tracking token check on RegulatoryReport compilation.  
    Violation Consequence: Report compilation rejected.  
  INV-03: Audit log retention MUST enforce a minimum 5-year data preservation policy strictly complying with FRA regulatory rules (Rule 24).  
    Business Rationale: Complies with statutory financial record retention laws.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated archival lifecycle policy disallowing premature deletion.  
    Violation Consequence: Deletion attempt blocked.

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-ENT

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-ENT  
CANONICAL NAME:      Entitlements & Subscription Management  
ARABIC NAME:         الصلاحيات وإدارة الاشتراكات  
CONTEXT CODE:        ENT  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      User Domain Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Supporting  
  Justification:     Entitlements & Subscription Management handles commercial subscription billing tiers (Free, Pro, Enterprise), feature entitlement matrices (`Entitlement`), market data feed licensing access rights, and API consumption quota enforcement (`Subscription`).  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for managing commercial user subscription tiers (`Subscription`), enforcing feature access entitlements (`Entitlement`), tracking API usage quotas, and gating real-time vs delayed market data access.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Management of commercial subscription plans and billing tier agreements (`Subscription`).  
  - Feature access entitlement matrices and paywall rules (`Entitlement`).  
  - Enforcement of real-time vs 15-minute delayed market data feed licensing access (Rule 36).  
  - Tracking and throttling of API call volume quotas per tier (Rule 37).  
  - Subscription tier lifecycle management (Free, Pro, Enterprise upgrades and renewals).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - User identity account creation or password credentials (owned strictly by `CTX-IDN`).  
  - Regulatory investment policy rules or pre-trade order blocking (owned strictly by `CTX-COMP`).  
  - Primary processing of credit card transactions (delegated to external payment gateway).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) & Product Monetization Director  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  All User Profiles, Beginner Investor, Active Trader, Enterprise B2B Partner, Platform Administrator  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `Subscription` (BDD Sec 9 Object 37) — Commercial tier agreement detailing plan status, billing cycle, and expiration date.  
  - `Entitlement` (BDD Sec 9 Object 38) — Feature access matrix defining allowed capabilities and rate limit quotas.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `ENT-SUB-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 8) — Subscription Tier Entitlement Enforcement (Primary Owner).  
  - `ENT-SUB-002` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 8) — API Volume Quota Enforcement (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `ENT_SUBSCRIPTION_ACTIVATED` — Triggered when a new commercial subscription plan is activated.  
  - `ENT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` — Triggered when user API consumption exceeds tier limit.  
  - `ENT_TIER_UPGRADED` — Triggered when user upgrades subscription plan tier.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `IDN_USER_REGISTERED` — Consumed from `CTX-IDN` to initialize default Free tier subscription.  
  - Payment gateway payment success webhook receipts.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `Subscription`: Commercial tier agreement granting access to specific platform features and data feeds (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `Entitlement`: Feature access right defining permission to consume a capability or data stream.  
  - `Quota`: Maximum allowed volume of API requests or data queries per billing cycle.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 36: Real-time EGX price feeds require an active Pro or Enterprise subscription; Free tier accounts must be restricted to 15-minute delayed market data (BDD Sec 10 Rule 36).  
  - Rule 37: API consumption rate limits must block or throttle requests exceeding monthly subscription tier quotas (BDD Sec 10 Rule 37).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `Subscription`, `Entitlement`, and `Quota` represent commercial monetization concepts distinct from `User` and `Portfolio`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 36 (real-time vs delayed data feed licensing) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `ENT_SUBSCRIPTION_ACTIVATED`, `ENT_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`, and `ENT_TIER_UPGRADED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `Subscription` and `Entitlement` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Subscriptions operate on monthly/annual commercial billing cycles independently of daily trading sessions.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) & Product Monetization Director.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-IDN: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes user identity records to link subscriptions.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-MKT: Consumes entitlement decisions to route real-time vs 15-min delayed market data streams.  
  - CTX-SCRN: Consumes subscription tier entitlements to limit screener result export volume.  
  - CTX-UI: Consumes entitlements to render feature paywalls and upgrade prompts.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Enforces EGX official market data licensing redistribution rules, restricting real-time streaming data feeds to authorized Pro subscribers.  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:  
  Complies with exchange market data vendor licensing agreements and consumer subscription transparency laws.  

CURRENT STATE:  
  Phase 1 (EGX Target)  

FUTURE EVOLUTION:

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-ALRT

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-ALRT  
CANONICAL NAME:      Price & Risk Alert Evaluation  
ARABIC NAME:         تقييم تنبيهات الأسعار والمخاطر  
CONTEXT CODE:        ALRT  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      User Engagement Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Supporting  
  Justification:     Price & Risk Alert Evaluation continuously evaluates real-time market price ticks, volatility spikes, and portfolio risk breaches against user-configured threshold rules (`AlertRule`). It owns threshold condition evaluation math, producing breach alert triggers (`AlertTrigger`).  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for managing user price alert rules (`AlertRule`), evaluating real-time price tick arrivals against active threshold conditions, and firing idempotent breach alert events (`AlertTrigger`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Management of user-configured price and volatility alert threshold rules (`AlertRule`).  
  - Real-time condition evaluation math comparing price tick streams against active alert thresholds.  
  - Detection of price ceiling/floor breaches, percentage movements, and volume spike triggers (`AlertTrigger`).  
  - Idempotent alert trigger throttling to prevent duplicate alerts.  
  - User alert rule lifecycle management (Active, Triggered, Paused).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Multi-channel transport delivery mechanisms via Push, Email, or SMS (owned strictly by `CTX-NOTIF`).  
  - Quantitative Value-at-Risk (VaR) model calculations (owned strictly by `CTX-RISK`).  
  - Real-time market tick ingestion or OHLCV bar processing (owned strictly by `CTX-PRC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Lead Real-Time Alert Engine & User Engagement Architect  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Active Trader, Long-Term Investor, Portfolio Manager, All User Profiles  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `AlertRule` (BDD Sec 9 Object 31) — User-configured alert rule payload detailing target symbol, threshold price, and breach condition.  
  - `AlertTrigger` (BDD Sec 9 Object 32) — Operational breach trigger event payload dispatched upon threshold condition satisfaction.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `ENG-ALT-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 6) — Price & Volatility Alert Evaluation (Primary Owner).  
  - `ENG-ALT-002` (Scoped Shared Kernel — Primary user alert threshold evaluation owner in CTX-ALRT; transport dispatch aspect owned by CTX-NOTIF. Registered in Appendix A).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `ALERT_THRESHOLD_BREACHED` — Triggered when a price tick satisfies a user alert threshold rule.  
  - `ALERT_RULE_CREATED` — Triggered when a user establishes a new price alert threshold.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `MKT_TICK_RECEIVED` — Consumed from `CTX-PRC` to evaluate real-time price tick arrivals.  
  - `RISK_CONCENTRATION_BREACHED` — Consumed from `CTX-RISK` to trigger portfolio risk threshold alerts.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `AlertRule`: User-configured threshold condition governing price or risk alert triggers (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `AlertTrigger`: System event generated when a real-time price tick satisfies an alert condition.  
  - `IdempotentCooldown`: Minimum time window preventing repeated duplicate alert triggers for a single threshold breach.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 18: Price alert threshold evaluation must complete within sub-100ms of real-time price tick arrival (BDD Sec 10 Rule 18 SLA).  
  - Rule 21: Risk breach alerts must be evaluated immediately upon portfolio concentration cap violations (BDD Sec 10 Rule 21).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `AlertRule` and `AlertTrigger` represent real-time threshold condition concepts distinct from `Notification` and `MarketTick`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 18 (sub-100ms alert evaluation SLA) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `ALERT_THRESHOLD_BREACHED` and `ALERT_RULE_CREATED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `AlertRule` and `AlertTrigger` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Alert rules evaluate continuously on sub-100ms price tick streams independently of notification transport queues.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Lead Real-Time Alert Engine & User Engagement Architect.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-PRC: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes real-time price tick streams.  
  - CTX-RISK: Customer/Supplier | SOFT | Consumes quantitative risk breach events.

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-NOTIF (Multi-Channel Notification Dispatch):  
    Condition Evaluation vs Transport Mechanism Distinction:  
      `CTX-ALRT` (Alert Evaluation) owns the mathematical condition evaluation ("Has CIB crossed 60 EGP?"). It operates on sub-100ms in-memory market tick evaluation cycles to detect threshold breaches.  
      `CTX-NOTIF` (Notification Dispatch) owns the transport delivery mechanisms (Push via Firebase, Email via SendGrid, SMS via Twilio, In-App drawer) and user channel delivery preferences. It operates on transport network dispatch queues.  
    Language difference: `AlertRule` is a mathematical threshold condition; `Notification` is a delivered transport message.  
    Rule difference: Rule 18 (sub-100ms price tick evaluation SLA) vs notification channel routing rules.  
    Object difference: OWNS `AlertRule` and `AlertTrigger`; does NOT own `Notification` or `NotificationPreference`.  
    Event difference: Produces `ALERT_THRESHOLD_BREACHED`; does NOT produce `NOTIF_DISPATCHED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-ALRT` evaluates real-time tick arrival streams continuously; `CTX-NOTIF` manages transport delivery queues and user quiet-hour preferences.  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-PRC (Market Price Execution):  
    Language difference: `AlertRule` is a user-configured threshold preference; `MarketTick` is a raw price bar observation.  
    Rule difference: Rule 18 (alert threshold matching) vs pricing bar aggregation rules.  
    Object difference: OWNS `AlertRule`; does NOT own `Price` or `OHLCV`.  
    Event difference: Produces `ALERT_RULE_CREATED`; does NOT produce `MKT_EOD_PRICES_PUBLISHED`.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Alert rule evaluation MUST complete synchronously within sub-100ms of real-time price tick arrival (Rule 18 SLA).  
    Business Rationale: Ensures traders receive immediate notification of critical price movements during fast market sessions.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory in-memory streaming index validator with 100ms execution timeout cap.  
    Violation Consequence: Latency SLA breach log flagged.  
  INV-02: Alert threshold triggers MUST be idempotent — the same price threshold crossing MUST NOT dispatch duplicate notifications within a declared 60-second cooldown window.  
    Business Rationale: Prevents notification spamming during market price oscillation around a single threshold.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory idempotency key check on AlertTrigger dispatch.  
    Violation Consequence: Duplicate trigger suppressed.  
  INV-03: Alert rules MUST contain valid listed instruments exclusively; delisted assets MUST cause associated alert rules to automatically pause.  
    Business Rationale: Prevents dead alert rules from consuming system evaluation memory.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Instrument delisting event handler updating AlertRule status to Paused.  
    Violation Consequence: Alert rule paused.

It acts as the central transport delivery context.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for consuming system breach and alert events, applying user delivery channel preferences (`NotificationPreference`), rendering localized message templates, and executing multi-channel notification dispatches (`Notification`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Multi-channel delivery transport dispatch management (Push, Email, SMS, In-App drawer).  
  - User notification channel preferences and quiet hours management (`NotificationPreference`).  
  - Bilingual Arabic/English notification template rendering.  
  - Notification delivery status tracking (Dispatched, Delivered, Failed, Read) (`Notification`).  
  - External messaging gateway integration adapters (Firebase FCM, SendGrid, Twilio).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Real-time price threshold condition evaluation math (owned strictly by `CTX-ALRT`).  
  - Quantitative VaR risk breach calculation (owned strictly by `CTX-RISK`).  
  - Core user identity email/phone credential storage (owned strictly by `CTX-IDN`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of User Communications & Notification Channels  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  All User Profiles, Active Trader, Long-Term Investor, Portfolio Manager  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `Notification` (BDD Sec 9 Object 29) — Operational notification message record detailing channel, payload, recipient, and status.  
  - `NotificationPreference` (BDD Sec 9 Object 30) — User delivery configuration specifying enabled channels and quiet hours.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `ENG-ALT-002` (Scoped Shared Kernel — Primary transport dispatch owner in CTX-NOTIF; user alert threshold evaluation aspect owned by CTX-ALRT. Registered in Appendix A).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `NOTIF_DISPATCHED` — Triggered when a notification payload is handed off to transport gateway.  
  - `NOTIF_DELIVERY_FAILED` — Triggered when transport gateway reports delivery failure.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `ALERT_THRESHOLD_BREACHED` — Consumed from `CTX-ALRT` to dispatch price alert notifications.  
  - `RISK_CONCENTRATION_BREACHED` — Consumed from `CTX-RISK` to dispatch high-priority risk warnings.  
  - `AI_RECOMMENDATION_GENERATED` — Consumed from `CTX-REC` to dispatch personalized recommendation alerts.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `Notification`: Delivered message payload routed across a specific transport channel (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `ChannelPreference`: User configuration specifying push, email, or SMS preferences per alert type.  
  - `QuietHours`: Time window during which non-critical notifications are suppressed or queued.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 18: Critical price and risk alerts must dispatch push notifications within sub-500ms of breach event receipt (BDD Sec 10 Rule 18 SLA).  
  - Rule 38: Notifications must respect user locale preferences, rendering messages in declared language (Arabic/English) (BDD Sec 10 Rule 38).

  Justification:     Investor Community & Social Sharing manages user-generated social posts, community forum discussions, comments, and shared verified portfolio allocations (`CommunityPost`, `UserComment`, `SharedPortfolioView`). It fosters social engagement while strictly redacting absolute monetary balances.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for publishing user-generated social content (`CommunityPost`), managing investor discussion threads (`UserComment`), enforcing content moderation rules, and sharing anonymized portfolio asset allocations (`SharedPortfolioView`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - User-generated social post publishing and community forum feeds (`CommunityPost`).  
  - User discussion comment threads and social interactions (`UserComment`).  
  - Verified portfolio asset allocation sharing (percentage views only) (`SharedPortfolioView`).  
  - Automated content moderation filtering (spam detection, abusive language blocking).  
  - Investor social follower graphs and community profile views.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - External financial media news scraping or quantitative sentiment analysis (owned strictly by `CTX-SENT`).  
  - Actual capital position share quantity accounting or NAV calculation (owned strictly by `CTX-POS` / `CTX-PORT`).  
  - Core user account authentication or password credentials (owned strictly by `CTX-IDN`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Investor Community & Social Engagement  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Beginner Investor, Active Trader, Wealth Advisor, Community Moderator, All User Profiles  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `CommunityPost` — User-generated social post entity detailing text content, attached instrument tags, and likes.  
  - `UserComment` — Threaded comment entity attached to community posts or equity research reports.  
  - `SharedPortfolioView` — Anonymized portfolio asset allocation view displaying percentage breakdown exclusively.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `ENG-ALT-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 6 — Community Engagement Aspect — Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `COMM_POST_PUBLISHED` — Triggered when a new user community post is published.  
  - `COMM_PORTFOLIO_SHARED` — Triggered when a user shares a verified portfolio allocation view.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `PORT_NAV_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-PORT` to update shared portfolio allocation percentages.  
  - User social post submission UI actions.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `CommunityPost`: User-generated social content published to investor community feeds.  
  - `SharedPortfolioView`: Anonymized asset allocation view displaying percentage breakdown without monetary values.  
  - `ContentModeration`: Automated filter inspecting user posts for spam, abusive language, or illegal financial advice.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 3.2: User community posts sharing investment views operate strictly as social opinions and must carry explicit non-custodial disclaimer headers (BDD Sec 10 Rule 3.2).  
  - Rule 39: Shared portfolio allocation views must strictly redact all absolute monetary values (EGP amounts) to protect user financial privacy (BDD Sec 10 Rule 39).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `CommunityPost` and `SharedPortfolioView` represent user-generated social engagement concepts distinct from `SentimentScore` and `Portfolio`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 39 (monetary redaction for shared portfolios) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `COMM_POST_PUBLISHED` and `COMM_PORTFOLIO_SHARED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `CommunityPost`, `UserComment`, and `SharedPortfolioView` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Community posts operate on social publishing cadences independently of stock market trading sessions.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Investor Community & Social Engagement.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-PORT: Open Host Service | SOFT | Consumes portfolio asset weights for shared percentage allocation views.  
  - CTX-IDN: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes user identity handles for post attribution.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-UI: Consumes community feeds and comments for rendering social community tabs.  
  - CTX-SENT: Consumes platform internal community post streams as an additional sentiment data source.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Supports community discussion forums tailored for Egyptian retail investors discussing EGX listed equities, Nilex SME stocks, and local market trends in Egyptian Arabic.  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:  
  Complies with online content moderation laws and FRA rules prohibiting unlicensed financial advice in public social forums.  

CURRENT STATE:  
  Phase 1 (EGX Target)  

FUTURE EVOLUTION:  
  Will expand in Phase 2 to support regional MENA investor communities (Saudi stock forums) and verified top-performing investor leaderboards in Phase 3.

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-SENT (Financial News & Sentiment Analysis):  
    User-Generated Social Content vs External Media Scraping Distinction:  
      `CTX-COMM` (Investor Community) manages USER-GENERATED social content, community forum discussions, comments, and shared portfolio views created directly by Tradeora users.  
      `CTX-SENT` (Financial News & Sentiment) scrapes EXTERNAL financial news media outlets, third-party social feeds, and earnings call transcripts to compute quantitative sentiment polarity scores.  
    Language difference: `CommunityPost` is a user social discussion entry; `SentimentScore` is a quantitative polarity metric (-1.0 to +1.0).  
    Rule difference: Rule 39 (monetary redaction for shared portfolios) vs Rule 8 (verifiable sentiment source attribution).  
    Object difference: OWNS `CommunityPost` and `SharedPortfolioView`; does NOT own `NewsArticle` or `SentimentScore`.  
    Event difference: Produces `COMM_POST_PUBLISHED`; does NOT produce `SENT_SCORE_UPDATED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-COMM` operates on user social publishing interactions; `CTX-SENT` operates on continuous external news feed scraping queues.  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-PORT (Portfolio NAV):  
    Language difference: `SharedPortfolioView` is an anonymized percentage allocation representation; `Portfolio` is an active capital position container with monetary balances.  
    Rule difference: Rule 39 (monetary redaction) vs Rule 5 (pricing valuation).  
    Object difference: OWNS `SharedPortfolioView`; does NOT own `Portfolio` or `Position`.  
    Event difference: Produces `COMM_PORTFOLIO_SHARED`; does NOT produce `PORT_NAV_UPDATED`.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Shared portfolio views (`SharedPortfolioView`) MUST expose anonymized asset allocation percentages exclusively; absolute monetary balances (EGP amounts) MUST be strictly redacted (Rule 39).  
    Business Rationale: Protects user financial privacy and prevents wealth disclosure exposure.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory monetary redaction filter on SharedPortfolioView serialization.  
    Violation Consequence: Shared portfolio view publishing rejected.  
  INV-02: All user-generated community posts MUST pass automated text moderation filters checking for spam, abusive language, and illegal stock manipulation solicitation prior to public feed visibility.  
    Business Rationale: Maintains community quality and complies with digital content regulations.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated text moderation pipeline check on post submission.  
    Violation Consequence: Post held for manual moderator review.  
  INV-03: Community posts containing specific stock symbol tags MUST automatically attach non-custodial social opinion disclaimers (Rule 3.2).  
    Business Rationale: Clarifies that user community posts do not constitute official licensed financial advice.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory disclaimer banner attachment layer on CommunityPost rendering.  
    Violation Consequence: Disclaimer appended automatically.

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-NUDGE

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-NUDGE  
CANONICAL NAME:      Behavioral Nudges & Financial Literacy  
ARABIC NAME:         التوجيه السلوكي والتثقيف المالي  
CONTEXT CODE:        NUDGE  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      User Engagement Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Supporting  
  Justification:     Behavioral Nudges & Financial Literacy delivers timely educational behavioral bias warnings (overtrading alerts, panic selling warnings, FOMO prompts) and financial literacy micro-learning modules (`BehavioralNudge`, `LiteracyModule`). It provides engagement supporting features rather than core financial execution.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for detecting emotional behavioral bias patterns, delivering timely educational nudges (`BehavioralNudge`), and providing interactive financial literacy micro-learning content (`LiteracyModule`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Detection of investor behavioral bias patterns (overtrading, panic selling, disposition effect, FOMO).  
  - Delivery of non-intrusive educational behavioral nudges (`BehavioralNudge`).  
  - Interactive financial literacy micro-learning content and quiz modules (`LiteracyModule`).  
  - Tracking user financial literacy completion progress.  
  - Behavioral nudge effectiveness telemetry analytics.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Quantitative asset allocation or AI recommendation generation (owned strictly by `CTX-REC`).  
  - Pre-trade order compliance blocking or regulatory entitlement checks (owned strictly by `CTX-COMP`).  
  - Multi-channel push notification delivery transport (owned strictly by `CTX-NOTIF`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Investor Education & Behavioral UX Science  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Beginner Investor, Individual Investor, All User Profiles  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `BehavioralNudge` — Timely educational nudge prompt warning against emotional trading biases.  
  - `LiteracyModule` — Micro-learning educational lesson object covering capital market concepts.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `ENG-ALT-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 6 — Behavioral Nudge Aspect — Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `NUDGE_DELIVERED` — Triggered when a behavioral bias nudge prompt is rendered to the user.  
  - `LITERACY_MODULE_COMPLETED` — Triggered when a user completes a financial literacy lesson.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `PORT_POSITION_CLOSED` — Consumed from `CTX-POS` to detect panic-selling patterns.  
  - `EXEC_ORDER_FILLED` — Consumed from `CTX-EXEC` to monitor trading frequency for overtrading bias.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `BehavioralNudge`: Non-intrusive educational prompt alerting users to emotional decision biases (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `LiteracyModule`: Bite-sized interactive educational lesson covering investment fundamentals.  
  - `DispositionEffect`: Behavioral tendency to sell winning investments too early while holding losing investments too long.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 1: Behavioral nudges operate strictly as educational guidance and must present clear assumption disclosures (BDD Sec 10 Rule 1).  
  - Rule 3.2: Behavioral nudges operate in non-custodial educational advisory mode; nudges must NEVER block user trade execution rights (BDD Sec 10 Rule 3.2 & Constitution Principle 3.2).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `BehavioralNudge` and `LiteracyModule` represent educational engagement concepts distinct from `Recommendation` and `ComplianceRule`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 3.2 (non-custodial educational guidance, zero execution blocking) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `NUDGE_DELIVERED` and `LITERACY_MODULE_COMPLETED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `BehavioralNudge` and `LiteracyModule` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Nudges operate on user behavioral triggers and educational learning milestones independently of market sessions.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Investor Education & Behavioral UX Science.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-POS: Open Host Service | SOFT | Consumes position closing events for panic selling detection.  
  - CTX-EXEC: Open Host Service | SOFT | Consumes trade execution fills for overtrading rate detection.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-UI: Consumes behavioral nudges and literacy modules to render contextual education cards.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Delivers financial literacy content tailored for Egyptian retail investors, explaining EGX market trading mechanisms, T+2 settlement, and local tax rules in Egyptian Arabic.  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:  
  Complies with Constitution Principle 3.2 (Non-custodial advisory mode; educational nudges never block user execution rights).  

CURRENT STATE:  
  Phase 1 (EGX Target)  

FUTURE EVOLUTION:  
  Will expand in Phase 2 to support gamified financial literacy learning paths and AI-personalized behavioral coaching in Phase 3.

  INV-01: Behavioral nudges MUST operate in non-custodial educational advisory mode; nudges MUST NEVER block or restrict user trade execution rights (Rule 3.2 & Constitution Principle 3.2).

    Violation Consequence: Nudge delivery aborted if execution blocking is detected.

    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated trade frequency anomaly detector validator.  
    Violation Consequence: Overtrading nudge suppressed.  
  INV-03: Financial literacy modules (`LiteracyModule`) MUST present objective educational content disallowing promotional stock pitching.  
    Business Rationale: Guarantees educational neutrality and investor trust.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory educational content review pipeline.  
    Violation Consequence: Module publishing rejected.

  Why this is NOT part of CTX-COMM (Investor Community):  
    Private Survey vs Public Community Content Distinction:  
      `CTX-FEEDBACK` (User Feedback) manages private customer feedback surveys, NPS scores, and product satisfaction ratings submitted directly to product managers.  
      `CTX-COMM` (Investor Community) manages public user-generated social posts, community forum threads, and shared portfolio views visible to all platform users.  
    Language difference: `FeedbackSurvey` is a private product satisfaction survey; `CommunityPost` is a public social forum entry.  
    Rule difference: Rule 7 (feedback attribution) vs Rule 39 (monetary redaction for shared posts).  
    Object difference: OWNS `FeedbackSurvey` and `NPSScore`; does NOT own `CommunityPost` or `UserComment`.

    Language difference: `NPSScore` is a product satisfaction metric; `User` is an account identity entity.  
    Rule difference: Feedback data collection rules vs Rule 38 (authentication security).  
    Object difference: OWNS `FeedbackSurvey`; does NOT own `User` or `UserProfile`.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Feedback survey prompts MUST disallow interrupting active trade execution workflows or order placement screens.  
    Business Rationale: Prevents product surveys from interfering with critical financial trade transactions.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory UI context check blocking survey triggers on trade screens.  
    Violation Consequence: Survey prompt suppressed.  
  INV-02: NPS survey prompts MUST enforce a minimum 30-day cooldown interval per user to prevent survey fatigue.  
    Business Rationale: Maintains positive user experience and prevents prompt annoyance.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated cooldown timestamp validator.  
    Violation Consequence: Survey trigger blocked.  
  INV-03: User qualitative feedback comments MUST be stored with opt-in consent choices.  
    Business Rationale: Complies with user data privacy guidelines.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory consent flag check on survey submission.  
    Violation Consequence: Feedback comment rejected.

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-API  
CANONICAL NAME:      Enterprise API Gateway & Rate-Limiting  
ARABIC NAME:         بوابة واجهات البرمجة وإدارة المعدلات  
CONTEXT CODE:        API  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Platform Infrastructure Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Enterprise API Gateway & Rate-Limiting manages edge network routing, request parsing, authentication token verification, API rate limiting, and gateway security across all external and internal API requests (`ApiRoute`, `RateLimitRule`). It acts as the primary API access boundary.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for routing incoming API requests (`ApiRoute`), enforcing rate-limiting bucket rules (`RateLimitRule`), validating authentication tokens, and protecting upstream microservices from traffic surges.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Edge API request routing, path rewriting, and load balancing (`ApiRoute`).  
  - API rate-limiting enforcement algorithms (token bucket / leaky bucket) (`RateLimitRule`).  
  - JWT token verification and API client security validation.  
  - Request/response payload format validation at edge boundary.  
  - Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) and edge security header enforcement.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Commercial subscription billing plans or monetization pricing definitions (owned strictly by `CTX-ENT`).  
  - Primary user password authentication credentials or user account creation (owned strictly by `CTX-IDN`).  
  - In-memory data caching or database persistence (owned strictly by `CTX-CACHE` / `CTX-DATA`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Platform Infrastructure & API Gateway Engineering  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Platform Administrator, Enterprise B2B Partner, All API Clients  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `ApiRoute` — API endpoint routing rule mapping URI paths to upstream target microservices.  
  - `RateLimitRule` — Operational rate-limiting bucket policy defining allowed request rates per minute.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `ENT-SUB-002` (Scoped Shared Kernel — Primary API gateway rate-limiting owner in CTX-API; subscription tier quota definition aspect owned by CTX-ENT. Registered in Appendix A).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `API_REQUEST_ROUTED` — Triggered when an API request passes edge security and is dispatched upstream.  
  - `API_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` — Triggered when a client request exceeds rate-limiting limits at edge.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - Incoming HTTP/HTTPS and WebSocket request streams from client applications.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `ApiRoute`: Edge routing mapping client API URIs to internal microservice endpoints.  
  - `RateLimitRule`: Algorithmic bucket constraint restricting API request frequency per client key.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 37: Edge API gateway rate limiting must enforce sub-5ms routing overhead latency while throttling un-entitled requests (BDD Sec 10 Rule 37 SLA).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `ApiRoute` and `RateLimitRule` represent edge network routing concepts distinct from `Subscription` and `User`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 37 (API gateway rate limiting and SLA overhead) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `API_REQUEST_ROUTED` and `API_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `ApiRoute` and `RateLimitRule` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Gateway routing operates on real-time network request processing cycles (sub-5ms) independently of financial trading sessions.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Platform Infrastructure & API Gateway Engineering.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-ENT: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes tier entitlement permissions for rate-limiting rules.  
  - CTX-IDN: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes authentication token verification keys.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - All Downstream Contexts: Consumes routed, authenticated API request streams passed by gateway.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Routes real-time EGX market data WebSocket connections and B2B broker API traffic, enforcing sub-5ms gateway routing latency.

  Technical access governance and API infrastructure security compliance.

It provides fast transient state management.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for managing in-memory cache keys (`CacheKey`), enforcing TTL cache invalidation policies (`CachePolicy`), warming price caches, and accelerating read query throughput.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Distributed in-memory caching cluster management (Redis / Memcached) (`CacheKey`).  
  - Real-time market price tick cache storage and instant invalidation (`CachePolicy`).  
  - User session state caching and query result pre-computation caching.  
  - Cache TTL (Time-To-Live) expiration policy management.  
  - In-memory cache hit ratio telemetry tracking.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Persistent database storage or data lake parquet file archiving (owned strictly by `CTX-DATA`).  
  - Raw market tick ingestion or pricing bar aggregation (owned strictly by `CTX-PRC`).  
  - Primary user account authentication credential storage (owned strictly by `CTX-IDN`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Lead Infrastructure Performance & Caching Architect  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Platform Administrator, SRE Engineer, Performance Specialist  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `CacheKey` — In-memory cache entry key entity detailing namespace, value payload, and creation timestamp.  
  - `CachePolicy` — Operational caching policy payload defining TTL expiration limits and invalidation triggers.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `OPS-GOV-002` (Scoped Shared Kernel — Primary cache acceleration owner in CTX-CACHE; data ingestion aspect owned by CTX-DATA. Registered in Appendix A).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `CACHE_INVALIDATED` — Triggered when a cache key or namespace is invalidated due to price update or TTL expiry.  
  - `CACHE_WARMED` — Triggered when pre-computed query cache warming completes.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `MKT_EOD_PRICES_PUBLISHED` — Consumed from `CTX-PRC` to invalidate closing price cache entries.  
  - `IDN_PROFILE_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-IDN` to invalidate user profile session cache.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `CacheKey`: In-memory key reference mapping to volatile pre-computed data payloads in Redis (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `TTL`: Time-To-Live duration after which an in-memory cache key automatically expires.  
  - `CacheInvalidation`: Process clearing stale cached data upon fresh domain event receipt.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:

  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `CACHE_INVALIDATED` and `CACHE_WARMED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `CacheKey` and `CachePolicy` objects.

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-DATA (Data Pipeline Operations):  
    Volatile Cache vs Persistent Lake Distinction:  
      `CTX-CACHE` (In-Memory Caching) manages volatile in-memory transient state (Redis), sub-millisecond read query acceleration, and dynamic TTL cache invalidation.  
      `CTX-DATA` (Data Pipelines) manages persistent database ETL pipelines, parquet data lake files, and long-term batch ingestion storage.  
    Language difference: `CacheKey` is a volatile in-memory key payload; `DataPipeline` is a persistent ETL stream.  
    Rule difference: Rule 5 (synchronous price tick cache invalidation) vs Rule 24 (schema validation for persistent storage).  
    Object difference: OWNS `CacheKey` and `CachePolicy`; does NOT own `DataPipeline` or `IngestionJob`.  
    Event difference: Produces `CACHE_INVALIDATED`; does NOT produce `DATA_PIPELINE_INGESTED`.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Market price tick cache invalidation MUST trigger synchronously upon receiving fresh price tick updates from `CTX-PRC` (Rule 5).  
    Business Rationale: Prevents stale price quotes from being served to user interface read queries.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Synchronous event subscriber handler clearing market price cache keys.  
    Violation Consequence: Stale cache risk alert logged.  
  INV-02: All cached financial market data entries MUST carry an explicit TTL (Time-To-Live) expiration cap (maximum 60 seconds for live prices).  
    Business Rationale: Ensures automatic eviction of un-updated market price keys.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory TTL parameter check on CacheKey insertion.  
    Violation Consequence: Cache insertion rejected if TTL missing.  
  INV-03: Cache cluster failure MUST fail open, routing queries directly to primary database stores without crashing API execution.  
    Business Rationale: Protects platform API availability during Redis cache cluster node outages.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Circuit breaker pattern on cache client wrapper.  
    Violation Consequence: Fallback to primary database read.

### CONTEXT METADATA BLOCK — CTX-EXEC

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-EXEC  
CANONICAL NAME:      Order Routing & Execution Management  
ARABIC NAME:         توجيه وتنفيذ أوامر التداول  
CONTEXT CODE:        EXEC  
DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Future Expansion Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0 (Phase 2 Target Architecture)  
STATUS:              Approved (Phase 2 Execution Scope)  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Enabling  
  Justification:     Order Routing & Execution Management validates, formats, and routes user-authorized trade orders to licensed external brokerage APIs via Smart Order Routing (SOR) (`TradeOrder`, `ExecutionFill`, `BrokerAccountLink`). TRADEORA IS NOT A BROKER AND NEVER HOLDS CLIENT CASH OR CUSTODY SECURITIES. It acts strictly as a non-custodial execution routing bridge.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for validating user-authorized trade order parameters (`TradeOrder`), routing order execution payloads to user-connected licensed Egyptian brokerage APIs via Smart Order Routing (SOR), tracking order execution fill reports (`ExecutionFill`), and managing non-custodial broker account links (`BrokerAccountLink`).  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Validation of user-authorized trade order parameters (limit price, order quantity, validity duration) (`TradeOrder`).  
  - Non-custodial Smart Order Routing (SOR) to external licensed broker execution APIs.  
  - Order execution fill tracking, status updates, and execution report parsing (`ExecutionFill`).  
  - Management of non-custodial OAuth broker account linkage tokens (`BrokerAccountLink`).  
  - Pre-dispatch order parameter validation against broker exchange limits.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Cash custody, client deposit management, or securities clearing (Tradeora is NOT a licensed broker).  
  - Settled position quantity accounting or cost basis lot tracking (owned strictly by `CTX-POS`).  
  - Quantitative portfolio asset allocation synthesis (owned strictly by `CTX-REC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Broker Integration & Trade Execution Architecture  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Active Trader, Long-Term Investor, Licensed External Broker API Gateway  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `TradeOrder` — User-authorized order entity detailing symbol, side (BUY/SELL), quantity, limit price, order status, and broker routing ID.  
  - `ExecutionFill` — Broker execution fill report entity detailing filled quantity, execution price, fill timestamp, and broker commission.  
  - `BrokerAccountLink` — Non-custodial OAuth link token representing connected licensed brokerage account connection.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `EXC-SOR-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 12) — Broker Order Parameter Routing (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `EXEC_ORDER_ROUTED` — Triggered when a user-authorized order is validated and dispatched to broker API.  
  - `EXEC_ORDER_FILLED` — Triggered when broker API returns execution fill confirmation.  
  - `EXEC_ORDER_REJECTED` — Triggered when broker API rejects order execution.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `AI_RECOMMENDATION_ACCEPTED` — Consumed when a user explicitly approves an AI recommendation for trade execution.  
  - `PORT_REBALANCE_CONFIRMED` — Consumed when a user explicitly approves a portfolio rebalancing plan.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `TradeOrder`: User-authorized financial trade order payload routed to a licensed external broker API (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `ExecutionFill`: Official confirmation report from licensed broker indicating partial or full order execution fill.  
  - `SmartOrderRouting`: Algorithmic parameter router selecting optimal broker API endpoint for execution.  
  - `NonCustodialRouting`: Execution architecture passing orders directly to licensed brokers without Tradeora holding client funds.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 3.2: Trade orders MUST require explicit human confirmation prior to broker API dispatch; autonomous trade execution without user approval is strictly forbidden (BDD Sec 10 Rule 3.2 & Constitution Principle 3.2).  
  - Rule 14: Order execution settlement MUST enforce EGX T+2 settlement rules across all equity order lifecycles (BDD Sec 10 Rule 14).  
  - Rule 21: Pre-order dispatch parameter verification must enforce broker price collar and order quantity limits.  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `TradeOrder`, `ExecutionFill`, and `BrokerAccountLink` represent trade execution concepts distinct from `Position` and `Recommendation`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 3.2 (explicit human confirmation, zero autonomous execution) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `EXEC_ORDER_ROUTED`, `EXEC_ORDER_FILLED`, and `EXEC_ORDER_REJECTED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `TradeOrder`, `ExecutionFill`, and `BrokerAccountLink` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Trade orders operate on real-time execution routing cycles during exchange market open hours.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Broker Integration & Trade Execution Architecture.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-COMP: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes pre-trade compliance checks before order dispatch.  
  - CTX-PRC: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes live market price ticks for order limit validation.  
  - CTX-IDN: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes user identity credentials for broker OAuth authentication.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-POS: Consumes `EXEC_ORDER_FILLED` events to update active capital position quantities.  
  - Licensed External Broker APIs: Receives formatted order routing payloads for exchange execution.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Routes orders to licensed Egyptian brokerage APIs (e.g., Hermes, Thndr, CI Capital APIs), enforcing EGX daily price circuit breaker limits and T+2 settlement conventions.  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:  
  Tradeora operates strictly as a non-custodial technology routing provider under FRA regulations; Tradeora NEVER holds client funds or acts as a broker-dealer.  

CURRENT STATE:  
  Phase 2 Architecture Target  

FUTURE EVOLUTION:  
  Will expand in Phase 2 to support multi-broker FIX protocol connectivity and algorithmic TWAP/VWAP execution routing in Phase 3.

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Trade orders MUST require explicit human trader confirmation prior to broker API dispatch; autonomous trade execution without explicit user approval is strictly forbidden (Rule 3.2 & Constitution Principle 3.2).

    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory user cryptographic signature requirement on TradeOrder dispatch payload.

    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory T+2 settlement date calculator in ExecutionFill processor.  
    Violation Consequence: Fill processing rejected if settlement date misaligned.  
  INV-03: Tradeora platform MUST NEVER hold client cash or custody securities; execution routing is strictly a non-custodial broker API pass-through.  
    Business Rationale: Prevents regulatory liability as an unlicensed broker-dealer and maintains non-custodial architecture.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory non-custodial broker API token router.  
    Violation Consequence: Direct payment or custody holding attempt blocked.

It provides quantitative strategy validation.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for managing user trading strategy definitions (`TradingStrategy`), executing historical backtest simulation runs over market data time series (`BacktestResult`), and computing quantitative strategy risk/return metrics.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - User-configured rule-based trading strategy definitions and parameters (`TradingStrategy`).  
  - Historical backtest simulation execution engine enforcing zero look-ahead bias (Rule 40).  
  - Historical strategy backtest performance results (`BacktestResult`) (Sharpe ratio, max drawdown, win rate).  
  - Technical entry/exit trigger rule validation over historical price time series.  
  - Strategy rule optimization parameter sweeps.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Fundamental valuation discount models like DCF, DDM, or EV/EBITDA multiples (owned strictly by `CTX-MODEL`).  
  - Real-time live broker trade order routing or execution handoffs (owned strictly by `CTX-EXEC`).  
  - Real-time market tick ingestion or OHLCV bar aggregation (owned strictly by `CTX-PRC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Lead Quantitative Strategy Architect & Backtesting SRE  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Active Trader, Quantitative Analyst, Portfolio Manager  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `TradingStrategy` — User-configured trading strategy entity detailing entry rules, exit triggers, and indicator parameters.  
  - `BacktestResult` — Historical simulation run result payload detailing equity curve, Sharpe ratio, drawdown, and trade log.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `AI-REC-003` (Scoped Shared Kernel — Primary quantitative strategy owner in CTX-STRAT; order flow aspect owned by CTX-FLOW. Registered in Appendix A).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `STRAT_BACKTEST_COMPLETED` — Triggered when a historical strategy backtest simulation run completes.  
  - `STRAT_RULE_UPDATED` — Triggered when a trading strategy rule parameter is updated.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `MKT_EOD_PRICES_PUBLISHED` — Consumed from `CTX-PRC` for historical price time series simulation.  
  - `DATA_ETL_COMPLETED` — Consumed from `CTX-DATA` for historical data lake dataset availability.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `TradingStrategy`: Configured set of technical and fundamental rules governing automated strategy signals (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `BacktestResult`: Quantitative performance report resulting from simulating a strategy over historical price data.  
  - `LookAheadBias`: Flaw in backtesting where future data is inadvertently consumed at historical time step $t$.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 40: Historical strategy backtesting MUST strictly enforce zero look-ahead bias (BDD Sec 10 Rule 40 & Constitution Principle 4.40).  
  - Rule 18: Strategy backtest execution engine must process 5-year daily price series simulations within sub-2-second SLA (BDD Sec 10 Rule 18).

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-MODEL (Quantitative Financial Modeling):  
    Strategy Execution vs Fundamental Valuation Distinction:  
      `CTX-STRAT` (Strategy Builder) manages user-configured technical trading rules (`TradingStrategy`), historical backtest simulation runs over price time series (`BacktestResult`), zero look-ahead bias enforcement (Rule 40), and Sharpe/Drawdown performance metrics.  
      `CTX-MODEL` (Financial Modeling) manages fundamental valuation discount models (DCF, DDM, EV/EBITDA multiples), financial projections (`ValuationModel`), and WACC/growth assumptions (`ProjectionAssumption`).  
    Language difference: `TradingStrategy` is a rule-based trading setup; `ValuationModel` is an intrinsic cash flow valuation calculation.  
    Rule difference: Rule 40 (zero look-ahead bias) vs Rule 1 (DCF assumption disclosure).  
    Object difference: OWNS `TradingStrategy` and `BacktestResult`; does NOT own `ValuationModel` or `ProjectionAssumption`.  
    Event difference: Produces `STRAT_BACKTEST_COMPLETED`; does NOT produce `MODEL_VALUATION_UPDATED`.  
    Temporal lifecycle difference: `CTX-STRAT` operates on historical time series backtest runs; `CTX-MODEL` operates on quarterly financial statement updates.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Historical strategy backtesting MUST strictly enforce zero look-ahead bias (Rule 40); backtest calculations at timestamp $t$ MUST consume data published prior to timestamp $t$ exclusively.  
    Business Rationale: Guarantees realistic, non-misleading historical backtest simulation results.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory temporal data filter capping dataset access at historical simulation timestamp $t$.  
    Violation Consequence: Backtest run invalidated if future data leakage is detected.  
  INV-02: Strategy rules MUST validate indicator input parameters before initiating historical simulations to prevent division-by-zero or infinite loop execution bugs.  
    Business Rationale: Protects backtesting compute resources from invalid strategy parameter configurations.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Pre-execution strategy rule parameter validator.  
    Violation Consequence: Strategy backtest run rejected.  
  INV-03: Backtest performance metrics (Sharpe Ratio, Max Drawdown) MUST incorporate realistic transaction slippage and commission friction estimates.  
    Business Rationale: Ensures backtest returns reflect net real-world trading profitability.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory transaction cost deduction layer in equity curve calculation.  
    Violation Consequence: Backtest result flagged if transaction costs are omitted.

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-MODEL

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Differentiating  
  Justification:     Quantitative Financial Modeling & Valuation manages fundamental valuation models (Discounted Cash Flow DCF, Dividend Discount Model DDM, EV/EBITDA multiples), financial projections (`ValuationModel`), and growth/wacc assumptions (`ProjectionAssumption`). It provides quantitative intrinsic valuation models.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for managing fundamental equity valuation models (`ValuationModel`), executing mathematical DCF/DDM fair-value calculations, managing projection assumptions (`ProjectionAssumption`), and performing sensitivity scenario analysis.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Fundamental valuation model calculations (DCF, Dividend Discount Model DDM, EV/EBITDA multiples) (`ValuationModel`).  
  - Financial growth, discount rate (WACC), and terminal value assumptions (`ProjectionAssumption`).  
  - Fair value per share estimations and sensitivity scenario matrix generation.  
  - Transparent assumption disclosure rendering alongside calculated fair values.  
  - Automated valuation model recalibration upon new financial statement arrivals.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Technical trading entry/exit strategy rules or backtest simulations (owned strictly by `CTX-STRAT`).  
  - Raw financial statement accounting line-item ingestion or EAS ratios (owned strictly by `CTX-FUND`).  
  - Qualitative equity research narrative generation (owned strictly by `CTX-INSIGHT`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Quantitative Valuation & Financial Engineering  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Research Analyst, Portfolio Manager, Long-Term Investor, Wealth Advisor  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `ValuationModel` — Quantitative valuation entity detailing model type (DCF/DDM), fair-value estimate, WACC rate, and sensitivity matrix.  
  - `ProjectionAssumption` — Growth assumption payload detailing revenue growth rates, operating margin projections, and terminal growth.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `RES-FND-003` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 2) — Fair Value DCF Modeling (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `MODEL_VALUATION_UPDATED` — Triggered when a company fair-value calculation is updated.  
  - `ASSUMPTION_REVISED` — Triggered when a financial projection growth assumption is modified.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `FUND_STATEMENT_INGESTED` — Consumed from `CTX-FUND` to re-run DCF models on new financial statements.  
  - `MAC_INDICATOR_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-MAC` to adjust WACC rates based on central bank interest rates.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `ValuationModel`: Mathematical model computing intrinsic fair value based on discounted cash flow projections (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `ProjectionAssumption`: Explicit financial parameter defining revenue growth, margin, and discount rate expectations.  
  - `SensitivityMatrix`: Grid displaying fair-value changes across varying WACC and terminal growth assumptions.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 1: Valuation models MUST explicitly disclose all WACC discount rate and growth assumptions alongside calculated fair values (BDD Sec 10 Rule 1 & Constitution Principle 3.1).  
  - Rule 5: Valuation models must automatically update fair value estimates upon receipt of fresh quarterly financial filings (BDD Sec 10 Rule 5).

  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 1 (explicit valuation assumption disclosures) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `MODEL_VALUATION_UPDATED` and `ASSUMPTION_REVISED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `ValuationModel` and `ProjectionAssumption` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Valuation models operate on quarterly financial reporting cycles independently of intraday trading sessions.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Quantitative Valuation & Financial Engineering.

DOMAIN CLUSTER:      Strategy and Market Intelligence Cluster  
VERSION:             1.0  
STATUS:              Approved  

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Supporting  
  Justification:     Industry Sector Analytics & Peer Comparison manages sector performance heatmap aggregations, industry peer group comparisons, market-cap weighted sector index tracking (`SectorHeatmap`, `PeerComparison`), and sector capital rotation analytics. It provides sector intelligence.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for aggregating individual stock metrics into sector heatmaps (`SectorHeatmap`), managing industry peer comparison groups (`PeerComparison`), and tracking sector rotation trends.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Industry sector heatmap performance aggregations (`SectorHeatmap`).  
  - Industry peer group relative valuation comparison metrics (`PeerComparison`).  
  - Market-capitalization weighted sector index calculations.  
  - Sector capital flow rotation indicator tracking.  
  - EGX 18 official industry sector taxonomy mapping.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Single-company financial statement accounting or ratio definitions (owned strictly by `CTX-FUND`).  
  - Single-asset market price tick ingestion or OHLCV processing (owned strictly by `CTX-PRC`).  
  - Quantitative macroeconomic series tracking (owned strictly by `CTX-MAC`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Head of Sector & Industry Equity Intelligence  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Research Analyst, Portfolio Manager, Fund Manager, Active Trader  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `SectorHeatmap` — Aggregated sector performance entity detailing sector price movement, capital flow, and market-cap weight.  
  - `PeerComparison` — Comparative analytics entity ranking companies within an industry sector across valuation and profitability metrics.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `RES-SEC-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 2) — Sector Heatmap Aggregation (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `SECTOR_HEATMAP_UPDATED` — Triggered when sector heatmap performance metrics are re-calculated.  
  - `PEER_RANKING_CALCULATED` — Triggered when industry peer group rankings update.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `MKT_EOD_PRICES_PUBLISHED` — Consumed from `CTX-PRC` to calculate daily sector price performance.  
  - `FUND_STATEMENT_INGESTED` — Consumed from `CTX-FUND` to update sector average valuation ratios.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `SectorHeatmap`: Visual and quantitative representation of capital performance across industry sectors (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `PeerComparison`: Relative ranking of companies within the same industry sector across valuation ratios (P/E, P/B).  
  - `SectorRotation`: Movement of investor capital from one industry sector to another based on economic cycles.  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 15: Peer group comparison calculations must strictly enforce industry sector isolation, preventing cross-sector ratio comparisons (BDD Sec 10 Rule 15).  
  - Rule 18: Sector heatmap aggregations must recalculate within sub-100ms of real-time price tick arrivals during market open (BDD Sec 10 Rule 18 SLA).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `SectorHeatmap` and `PeerComparison` represent industry sector concepts distinct from `MarketTick` and `BalanceSheet`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 15 (strict sector isolation for peer group comparisons) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `SECTOR_HEATMAP_UPDATED` and `PEER_RANKING_CALCULATED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `SectorHeatmap` and `PeerComparison` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Sector heatmaps update continuously on market price arrivals independently of individual company financial reports.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Head of Sector & Industry Equity Intelligence.  
  CONFIRMED EVIDENCE COUNT: 6 / 6  

INTEGRATION DEPENDENCIES:  
  - CTX-PRC: Customer/Supplier | HARD | Consumes real-time stock prices for sector performance calculation.  
  - CTX-FUND: Open Host Service | HARD | Consumes financial ratios for peer group ranking.  

INTEGRATION CONSUMERS:  
  - CTX-UI: Consumes sector heatmaps and peer comparison tables for visual rendering.  
  - CTX-REC: Consumes sector rotation indicators for top-down AI recommendation weighting.  

EGX-SPECIFIC NOTES:  
  Aggregates sector heatmaps strictly across the 18 official EGX sector classifications (Banking, Real Estate, Industrial Goods, Basic Resources, Financial Services, etc.).  

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS:  
  Standard analytical industry aggregation; zero regulatory advice liability.  

CURRENT STATE:  
  Phase 1 (EGX Target)  

FUTURE EVOLUTION:  
  Will expand in Phase 2 to support cross-market MENA sector comparisons (Saudi Tadawul vs EGX sectors) and sub-industry micro-clustering in Phase 3.  

CAPABILITY VERSION:  
  Initial Version: 1.0 | Last Updated: 2026-07-21 | Status: Active

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-FUND (Financial Research):  
    Cross-Company Sector Aggregation vs Single-Company Accounting Distinction:  
      `CTX-SECT` (Sector Analytics) manages cross-company sector heatmap aggregations (`SectorHeatmap`), industry peer group comparisons (`PeerComparison`), and market-cap weighted sector index calculations across the EGX 18 sectors.  
      `CTX-FUND` (Financial Research) manages single-company balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements, and EAS accounting ratios (`FinancialStatement`, `FinancialRatio`).  
    Language difference: `SectorHeatmap` is an industry-wide capital flow view; `FinancialStatement` is a single company's accounting filing.  
    Rule difference: Rule 15 (strict sector peer isolation) vs Rule 24 (EAS accounting compliance).  
    Object difference: OWNS `SectorHeatmap` and `PeerComparison`; does NOT own `FinancialStatement` or `FinancialRatio`.  
    Event difference: Produces `SECTOR_HEATMAP_UPDATED`; does NOT produce `FUND_STATEMENT_INGESTED`.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: Peer group comparison calculations MUST strictly enforce industry sector isolation, preventing cross-sector ratio comparisons (Rule 15).  
    Business Rationale: Prevents mathematically misleading peer comparisons (e.g. comparing a bank P/E with a real estate developer P/E).  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory sector code matcher in PeerComparison generator.  
    Violation Consequence: Peer comparison calculation aborted if sectors differ.  
  INV-02: Sector heatmaps MUST calculate market-capitalization weighted performance values rather than simple un-weighted arithmetic averages.  
    Business Rationale: Ensures sector heatmap accurately reflects true capital movement impact.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Market-cap weighting formula enforcer in SectorHeatmap aggregator.  
    Violation Consequence: Un-weighted sector calculation rejected.  
  INV-03: EGX sector classifications MUST map 100% of listed equities to valid official EGX 18 sector codes; unassigned equities MUST be assigned to "Unclassified" holding bucket.  
    Business Rationale: Guarantees complete sector coverage without missing listed instruments.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory sector mapping validator on instrument onboarding.  
    Violation Consequence: Instrument assigned to holding bucket.

CONTEXT ID:          CTX-INSIGHT

DOMAIN CLASSIFICATION:  
  Classification:    Core Differentiating  
  Justification:     AI Automated Insight & Narrative Generation manages automated synthesis of bilingual Arabic/English equity research summaries, daily market intelligence briefs, financial news summaries (`ResearchReport`, `MarketBrief`), and natural language financial narrative generation. It provides automated AI financial research synthesis.  

BUSINESS PURPOSE:  
  This context is responsible for synthesizing automated equity research reports (`ResearchReport`), generating daily market intelligence briefs (`MarketBrief`), rendering localized financial narrative summaries, and attaching mandatory non-custodial AI disclaimers.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT OWNS:  
  - Automated equity research report synthesis and fair-value summary cards (`ResearchReport`).  
  - Daily pre-market opening intelligence brief compilation (`MarketBrief`).  
  - Bilingual Arabic/English financial narrative generation using zero-hallucination grounded prompts.  
  - Attachment of mandatory non-custodial advisory disclaimer headers (Principle 3.2 & Rule 1).  
  - Citation tracking linking narrative claims directly to verified underlying financial statements and news.  

SCOPE — WHAT THIS CONTEXT DOES NOT OWN:  
  - Ad-hoc conversational chat query responses or user prompt dialogs (owned strictly by `CTX-NLQ`).  
  - Personalized asset allocation trade recommendations or portfolio rebalancing proposals (owned strictly by `CTX-REC`).  
  - Fundamental DCF fair-value mathematical calculations (owned strictly by `CTX-MODEL`).  

BUSINESS OWNER:  
  Lead AI Financial Narrative Architect & Content Intelligence Lead  

PRIMARY ACTORS:  
  Beginner Investor, Long-Term Investor, Active Trader, Financial Advisor  

OWNED BUSINESS OBJECTS:  
  - `ResearchReport` — Structured AI-synthesized equity research report entity detailing fair-value summary, moat evaluation, and key risk factors.  
  - `MarketBrief` — Daily market summary narrative detailing index movements, top sector gainers/losers, and key economic announcements.  

OWNED CAPABILITIES:  
  - `AI-RES-001` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 3) — Equity Research Report Synthesis (Primary Owner).  
  - `AI-RES-002` (BCM Sec 3 Domain 3) — Daily Market Brief Compilation (Primary Owner).  

PRODUCED EVENTS:  
  - `INSIGHT_REPORT_GENERATED` — Triggered when an automated equity research report synthesis completes.  
  - `MARKET_BRIEF_COMPILED` — Triggered when a daily market brief is published for users.  

CONSUMED EVENTS:  
  - `MODEL_VALUATION_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-MODEL` to trigger research report narrative updates.  
  - `SENT_SCORE_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-SENT` to incorporate news sentiment polarity into narratives.  
  - `MAC_INDICATOR_UPDATED` — Consumed from `CTX-MAC` to include macroeconomic context in daily market briefs.  

UBIQUITOUS LANGUAGE TERMS:  
  - `ResearchReport`: AI-synthesized equity research summary combining fundamental models, news sentiment, and moat analysis (UL Sec 2.1).  
  - `MarketBrief`: Daily pre-market opening financial summary note providing macro and sector context.  
  - `GroundedPrompt`: LLM prompt architecture strictly restricting generation to verified retrieved context blocks (zero-hallucination).  

BUSINESS RULES OWNED:  
  - Rule 1: AI-generated financial narratives MUST carry explicit "AI-generated financial analysis — operates in non-custodial advisory mode and does not constitute official financial advice" disclaimer headers (BDD Sec 10 Rule 1 & Constitution Principle 3.2).  
  - Rule 38: Generated narratives MUST be rendered natively in recipient's preferred locale language (Arabic/English) with RTL support (BDD Sec 10 Rule 38).  

DISCOVERY EVIDENCE:  
  - Language Evidence:   YES — `ResearchReport` and `MarketBrief` represent automated research narrative concepts distinct from `Recommendation` and `ChatMessage`.  
  - Rule Evidence:       YES — Rule 1 (mandatory AI disclaimer header) applies explicitly here.  
  - Event Evidence:      YES — Produces `INSIGHT_REPORT_GENERATED` and `MARKET_BRIEF_COMPILED`.  
  - Object Evidence:     YES — Exclusive owner of `ResearchReport` and `MarketBrief` objects.  
  - Lifecycle Evidence:  YES — Research reports update on fundamental valuation changes or daily pre-market schedules.  
  - Ownership Evidence:  YES — Accountable owner is Lead AI Financial Narrative Architect & Content Intelligence Lead.

  - CTX-MAC: Open Host Service | SOFT | Consumes macroeconomic series for daily briefs.

[BOUNDARY JUSTIFICATION]  
  Why this is NOT part of CTX-NLQ (Natural Language Querying):  
    Proactive Research Synthesis vs Reactive Conversational Chat Distinction:  
      `CTX-INSIGHT` (Narrative Generation) proactively synthesizes structured equity research reports (`ResearchReport`) and daily market briefs (`MarketBrief`) based on schedule or fundamental valuation updates.  
      `CTX-NLQ` (Natural Language Querying) reactively processes ad-hoc user conversational chat queries ("What is CIB's PE ratio?") and maintains multi-turn conversation sessions (`ChatSession`).  
    Language difference: `ResearchReport` is a publication-ready research document; `ChatMessage` is an ad-hoc conversational dialog turn.  
    Rule difference: Rule 1 (mandatory AI disclaimer header) vs Rule 7 (conversational session management).  
    Object difference: OWNS `ResearchReport` and `MarketBrief`; does NOT own `ChatSession` or `ChatMessage`.  
    Event difference: Produces `INSIGHT_REPORT_GENERATED`; does NOT produce `NLQ_RESPONSE_GENERATED`.  

[BUSINESS INVARIANTS]  
  INV-01: AI-generated financial narratives and automated research summaries MUST carry explicit disclaimer headers ("AI-generated financial analysis — operates in non-custodial advisory mode and does not constitute official financial advice") complying with Principle 3.2 & Rule 1.  
    Business Rationale: Ensures absolute legal transparency and complies with non-custodial advisory principles.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Mandatory disclaimer header injection layer on ResearchReport and MarketBrief serialization.  
    Violation Consequence: Report generation aborted if disclaimer header is missing.  
  INV-02: Generated research summaries MUST cite verified data sources, forbidding un-sourced quantitative assertions (Principle 3.1 zero-hallucination mandate).  
    Business Rationale: Eliminates AI hallucinations and maintains financial research integrity.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated citation validator verifying narrative data points against retrieved context.  
    Violation Consequence: Report held for manual review if un-cited claims are detected.  
  INV-03: Daily MarketBrief compilation MUST complete and publish prior to 9:30 AM Cairo time (30 minutes before EGX market open).  
    Business Rationale: Ensures users receive morning intelligence before active trading begins.  
    Enforcement Mechanism: Automated pre-market cron scheduler.  
    Violation Consequence: Market brief delay alert logged.
